## GENERAL REMARKS - BRAKES  [939003520]
- Path: Descriptions > 33 BRAKES > GENERAL REMARKS - BRAKES
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939003520

#### SPECIFICATIONS
The braking system is the power assisted hydraulic type, comprising two crossover, independent ciruits (each circuit acting on one front wheel and the diagonally opposite rear wheel) to ensure braking and stability even if one of the circuits fails.
The system is also equipped with the following assisted braking and steering systems:
- ABS: anti-lock brakes;
- EBD: electronic brakeforce distribution between the front and rear wheels;
- ASR: traction control via management of the brakes and engine control unit;
- MSR: engine brake control by means of engine control unit management;
- VDC: vehicle electronic stability control;
- HBA: automatic increase in braking pressure during emergency braking;
- Hill Holder: assisted hill start system that keeps the vehicle braked while parked on slopes and automatically releases the brakes when the driver wishes to set off.
The vehicle is equipped with an ABS/EBD brake control system.
The ABS is fitted parallel to the hydraulic braking system so that should it not work braking would still be guaranteed.
The ABS incorporates the EBD function (Electronic Brake force Distribution) therefore the hydraulic system does not have a rear load proportioning valve.

#### ABS/EBD SYSTEM

##### View of assembly
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939001990.jpg]
1. ABS/EBD control unit
2. Left front wheel sensor
3. Right front wheel sensor
4. Right rear wheel sensor
5. Left rear wheel sensor
6. EBD warning light
7. ABS warning light

##### Specifications
The ABS control unit implements the ABS and EBD functions.
The ABS control unit is connected to the front wiring, the system cable loom is incorporated with the engine compartment cable loom.
> Note: The pin out of the ABS control unit with EBD is different from control units with ASR and VDC functions.

##### Composition
The ABS consists of:
- an electronic control unit integral with the hydraulic control unit
- an electrohydraulic control unit that modulates braking pressure by means of eight solenoids, two for each wheel
- four active sensors that detect the angular rotating speed of the wheels.
- wiring with specific connector

##### Operation

###### Introduction
The electronic control unit processes signals from the active sensors and brake light control switch. It identifies the wheel or wheels with a tendency to lock (maximum slip between wheel and road surface) by means of the control unit software and modulates the brake fluid pressure selectiely for the front wheels and in tandem for the rear wheels (select-low function).
The ABS modulates brake pressure in accordance with three basic stages:
- pressure maintenance stage
- pressure reduction stage
- pressure increase stage
If operation is requested, the ABS stays active at speeds greater than 2.7 km/h. After that, it cuts out to allow the car to stop. After each key ON and when a speed of 6 km/h is exceeded, the control unit carries out an operation check on the solenoids and pump engine. The control unit also tests the sensors when a speed of 12 km/h is exceeded.

###### Operating logics
PRESSURE INCREASE STAGE WITHOUT ABS OPERATION
When the brake pedal is pressed, the electronic control unit (1):
- does not supply load solenoid (N.O.) (2)
- does not supply discharge solenoid (N.C.) (3)
The pressure generated by brake pump (4) therefore reaches brake calipers (5) without undergoing changes.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939001991.jpg]
EXAMPLE OF ABS OPERATION
Pressure maintenance stage
Control unit (1):
- supplies load solenoid (N.O.) (2)
- does not supply discharge solenoid (N.C.) (3)
Therefore the hydaulic connection between the brake pump (4a) and brake calliper (5) is broken.
The pressure in brake caliper (5) remains constant even when pressure on the brake pedal is increased.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939001992.jpg]
Pressure reduction stage
Control unit (1):
- supplies load solenoid (N.O.) (2)
- does not supply discharge solenoid (N.C.) (3)
The hydraulic connection between brake pump (4) and brake caliper (5) is broken and discharge solenoid (3) opens and brings brake caliper (5) into communication with low pressure accumulator (6) and scavenger pump (7).
Control unit (1) also supplies motor (8) controlling scavenging pump (7) to restore the fuel taken to the brake callipers (5) to the main circuit.
The fluid flows through high pressure accumulator (9) and restriction (10) that performs a damping function.
The system is equipped with a check valve (11) fitted in parallel with load solenoid (2) that allows fast reduction of pressure in brake caliper (5) during brake pedal release.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939001993.jpg]
Pressure increase stage
Control unit (1):
- does not supply load solenoid (N.O.) (2)
- does not supply discharge solenoid (N.C.) (3)
The fluid taken into the main circuit is then free to return to brake caliper (5) and increase the pressure acting on the brake caliper.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939001994.jpg]
EBD function (Electronic Brake-Force distribution)
The EBD function controls the distribution of brakeforce and therefore replaces the conventional mechanical load proportioning valve to allow:
- independent action on the rear brake callipers
- improved brakeforce distribution
- perform in optimum manner under any load condition (static or dynamic), driving conditions (in a straight line or corner) and when the vehicle is in any state of repair (worn tyres, brakes and suspension)
- implementation of a strategy that follows the ideal distribution curve.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939001995.jpg]
Fa - Front axle brake force
Fp - Rear axle brake force
A - Distribution curve implemented by the brake system
B - Ideal distribution curve
C - Distribution curve implemented by a conventional hydraulic load proportional valve
D - Distribution curve implemented by the EBD function
EBD function failure is indicated by simultaneous activation of:
- ABS warning light;
- low brake flud and/or handbrake on warning light.
Under these conditions, the car must be driven with extreme caution to the nearest authorised workshop to check the system.
RECOVERY
The electronic control unit is equipped with a safety circuit that monitors ABS efficiency.
With key on, the safety circuit carries out an initial autotest for 4 seconds to check:
- electronic control unit operation;
- solenoid operation.
Every time the car starts off from a standstill, the safety circuit checks for signals from active sensors.
When the car is in motion, the safety circuit works as follows:
- continually compares angular wheel speed with the calculated reference speed
- checks memory condition
- checks operation of both relays, the solenoids and the pump motor
- constantly monitors battery voltage.
- monitors the efficiency of the brake pedal switch.
If the safety circuit detects one or more faults in system components during the check stage, the safety circuit operates as follows:
- deactivates the ABS while still guaranteeing operation of the conventional braking system
- indicates the fault status to the driver by turning on a warning light on the control panel.

#### ASR TRACTION CONTROL/ADJUSTMENT DEVICES
In addition to the ABS EBD system, the vehicle is also equipped with a system for controlling the stability of the vehicle VDC which includes the traction control system ASR.
The VDC system, in particular, thanks to slewing sensors and steering wheel angle sensors, guarantees the monitoring of the dynamics of the entire vehicle thereby improving active safety.

##### View of assembly
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939001996.jpg]
1. ABS/VDC control unit
2. Steering angle sensor
3. Engine management control unit
4. Left front wheel sensor.
5. Slewing/lateral acceleration sensor
6. Right front wheel sensor.
7. ASR off button with warning light
8. Right rear wheel sensor.
9. Left rear wheel sensor.
10. VDC warning light
11. EBD warning light
12. ABS warning light

##### Specifications
Driving a vehicle in all conditions where the physical limits of grip and, consequently, stability may be reached can be a difficult task for the average driver therefore in order to further improve safe driving conditions an electronic system capable of assisting the driver with this difficult task is available.
The systems currently employed to ensure safer driving in particular conditions are mainly the A.B.S. which controls braking and the T.C. and systems which control traction during acceleration through action on the brakes (T.C.) and traction/drive torque during acceleration and release through action on the brakes and on the engine control system motorized throttle (A.S.R./M.S.R.).
The VDC system includes all the above listed functions ensuring optimum dynamic control of the vehicle with the addition of specific sensors:
- steering angle sensor on the steering wheel
- slewing/lateral acceleration sensor at the centre of gravity under the centre tunnel.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939001997.jpg]
µ - Wheel grip
S - Slipping
A - EBD intervention area
A - ABS intervention area
C - VDC intervention area
1 - Lateral force curve
2 - Longitudinal force curve
As can be seen from the grip/slipping diagram, the area covered by the VDC system is larger than that covered by a conventional ABS/EBD system.
The VDC system cannot be switched off as it is a safety system; the A.S.R./M.S.R. function, on the other hand, can be switched off via the button in the centre console.
> Note: To ensure the drive of the vehicle (drive wheels) with snow chains fitted or in particular road surface conditions (snow, ice, deep mud, sand or gravel) it is advisable to switch the A.S.R. off.
The intervention of the VDC system is signalled by a special warning light in the instrument panel node

##### Composition
The VDC system consists of:
- an electro-hydraulic/electronic A.B.S. control unit (with an VD logic)
- interface with the C-CAN line, resident in the ABS control unit for communication with the engine control unit, steering angle sensor and lateral acceleration sensor;
- Magnetic-resistive type wheel speed sensors
- steering angle sensor with C.A.N. interface (steering angle sensor)
- slewing/lateral acceleration sensor in one piece integral with the CAN interface;
- brake fluid pressure sensor incorporated in the A.B.S. control unit
- ABS-EBD-VDC warning light in the instrument panel controlled via the dedicated serial line
- A.S.R. off switch with a warning light in the button

##### Operation
The VDC continuously recognizes a loss in grip for the wheels, both longitudinal and transverse, in all driving conditions from braking to acceleration in order to ensure the direction and the stability of the vehicle.
The management of the VDC system is entrusted to the A.B.S. electronic control unit, integrated with a special electro-hydraulic control unit, that allows action on the braking system independently of the action of the user.
The control unit processes the following signals:
- steering wheel rotation angle
- lateral acceleration and slewing
- engine operating conditions:
- wheel rpm
- hydraulic braking system pressure
and uses special algorithms in the electronic control unit software to obtain the figures for the dynamic control of the vehicle:
- longitudinal and transverse sliding between the wheels and the road surface
- axle drift.
Using these figures the system interprets the effective dynamics of the vehicle; having identified all the critical conditions due to environmental factors (e.g. surface with poor grip) or any errors made by the user (e.g. panic situations) and with subsequent intervention on the brakes and the drive torque, the vehicle is restored to good driving conditions.
The system interfaces with:
- NCM for drive torque adjustment via the C-CAN line;
- control panel via a serial line for warning light control.
The system is combined with a power unit with a specific brake pump; in addition, the pipes between the brake pump and the A.B.S. control unit have a Titaflex insert because the diameter of the pipe (6mm) is larger than regular pipes (4 mm); this is designed to prevent adverse effects on the operation of the VDC at low brake fluid temperatures.
There is a dedicated line (line K) for the diagnosis of the system.
The VDC system switches on automatically when the vehicle is started up and cannot be switched off by the user; the button in the centre console only switches off the A.S.R. function and only when advisable.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939001998.jpg]
INPUT SIGNALS:
- Wheel speed sensors (from direct line) (3)
- Three stage normally open brake pedal switch (from direct line) (4)
- ASR off button (from direct line) (5)
- engine control unti (2) (from C-CAN line);
- throttle angle position (7) (from C-CAN line) (only for JTS);
- control panel (12);
- Warning light status signal (from dedicated serial line) (10)
- Slewing sensor (rotation of vehicle on vertical axis) (from C-CAN line) (9)
- Lateral acceleration sensor (from C-CAN line) (9)
- Steering angle/steering wheel rotation sensor (from C-CAN line) (11)
- Hydraulic system pressure sensor (from direct line) (1)
OUTPUT SIGNALS:
- Brake pressure modulation control (13)
- Ignition advance reduction control (from C-CAN line) (8) (only for JTS);
- Engine power management control (from C-CAN line) (7) (only for JTS);
- Ignition advance reduction control (from C-CAN line) (15) (only for JTS);
- Engine power management control (from C-CAN line) (14) (only for JTD);
- VSO signal (vehicle speed) (12)
- VDC/ASR-ABS-EBD warning liight control on panel (from dedicated serial line) (10);
- ASR off LED (6)

###### Operating logics
As stated previously, in addition to controlling the slipping of the vehicle in a lengthwise direction, the VDC system also controls slipping in a sideways direction and, as a result, controls the lateral stability of the vehicle.
The lateral stability of a vehicle is the result of the reaction of the tyres to lateral forces due to increased centrifugal force.
The action of the lateral forces produce a variation in the drift angle of the wheels and, consequently, a variation in the axle drift (drift angle = difference between the desired route and the effective route).
The lateral forces do not, however, act equally on all four wheels because they are not subject to the same load conditions, in effect the load on the wheel differs depending on the situation the wheel is in, namely:
- acceleration (lightening of the front axle and loading of the rear axle)
- braking (loading of the front axle and lightening of the rear axle)
- bend to the right/left (loading or the outer wheels and lightening of the inner wheels)
- accelerating/decelerating round a bend (combination of the cases mentioned above).
It is obvious that if the lateral forces acting on the individual wheels vary, there will also be a variation in the forces acting on the vehicle axles; consequently the lateral forces acting on the front axle overcome those on the rear axle and viceversa determining a rotation (moment) on the vehicle axis of the vehicle (slewing axis).
The moment of slewing affects the behaviour of the vehicle producing either understeer or oversteer.
Understeer for a vehicle is when, with increasing lateral acceleration, the drift angle for the front axle increases greatly compared with that of the rear axle. In this case, the vehicle tends to go straight ahead (take the curve wide) when cornering.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939001999.jpg]
Oversteer for a vehicle is when, with increasing transverse acceleration, the drift angle for the rear axle increases greatly compared with that of the front axle. In this case the vehicle tends to turn around on itself (the rear axle tends to go straight, therefore the vehicle "hugs" the bend).
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939002000.jpg]
In order to keep the effect of lateral forces under control and limit the slewing moment, the A.B.S. control unit must firstly calculate the behaviour of vehicle set by the driver using:
- steering wheel angle sensor
- accelerator pedal position;
- brake circuit pressure
after which the control unit should check the actual behaviour of the vehicle through:
- The wheel sensors (vehicle speed/wheel speed),
- lateral acceleration sensor
- slewing sensor.
The control unit is able to:
- detecting actions carried out by the user, in effect, through the position of the steering wheel it checks the number of degrees (wide radius or narrow radius bends) and the speed for rotating the steering wheel (sharp or gentle rotations) and, using the position of the throttle and the brake pressure when accelerating or braking, how the user is taking the bend or deviating from the straight path.
- detecting the actual behaviour of the vehicle given the environmental variables, e.g. slippery surface, reaction of the vehicle to incorrect manoeuvres by the user, etc., in order to identify the moment of slewing and the lateral sliding of the axles via the sensors on the four wheels and the slewing/lateral acceleration sensor.
These two operations are necessary to superimpose the mathematical model mapped in the control unit on the effective behaviour of the vehicle in order to identify the state in which the vehicle is in (understeer or oversteer) and decide the action for the brakes and the engine
UNDERSTEER ON CORNERS
The control unit verifies the presence of understeer (mainly from the drift of the front axle), corrects the behaviour of the vehicle, braking the inner wheels round the bend in order to create an opposing moment which will lead the vehicle towards the centre of the bend and, possibly, reducing the drive torque.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939002001.jpg]
OVERSTEERIN ON CORNERS
In the presence of understeer (mainly from the drift of the rear axle) the control unit corrects the behaviour of the vehicle, braking the outer front wheel round the bend in order to create an opposite slewing moment, if necessary increasing the drive torque.
> Note: The system intervenes before the oversteer and understeer values are too high in order to limit the corrective measures that have to be taken which could make handling difficult.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939002002.jpg]
ABRUPT VARIATIONS FROM A STRAIGHT PATH (SLALOM/OVERTAKING)
In the case of sharp variations from the path (e.g. overtaking, slalom), the control unit identifies possible oversteer and understeer conditions and corrects the path of the vehicle acting as described in the cases mentioned previously.
ABRUPT VARIATION FROM A STRAIGHT PATH (DRIVING OVER DIFFERENT SURFACES)
The control unit is capable of detecting deviations in the path and the prevalence of axle drift, correcting the path through suitable action on the brakes and the engine.
ABRUPT ACCELERATION/DECELERATION
The control unit uses the A.S.R./M.S.R. strategy also controlling the lateral acceleration of the vehicle and, as a result, regulating the action on the front and rear brakes and on the engine torque in a more complete way than on vehicles with ASR only.
INTERVENTION - INTERVENTION TIMES UNDER CONDITIONS WHERE ROAD SURFACE GRIP IS GOOD (ASPHALT)
For JTS versions:
Engine torque reduction by the engine management control unit through the alteration of the ignition advances, 6/100 of a second after the slipping limit is exceeded.
A further reduction in torque through a decrease in the throttle opening (by the engine management control unit through the motorized throttle body after 15/100 of a second).
Intervention of the hydraulic system (braking force on the drive wheels) after 2/10 of a second.
For JTD versions:
Torque reduction via the engine control unit by reducing fuel flow, after 6/10 second.
Intervention of the hydraulic system (braking force on the drive wheels) after 2/10 of a second.
OPERATION UNDER CONDITIONS OF POOR GRIP
The system is capable of recognizing these conditions by comparing the acceleration of the drive wheels with the torque transmitted by the engine (engine load from the engine management control unit).
The system behaves in the same way as for both drive wheels slipping in good road grip conditions (asphalt) and the intervention levels are at the lower limit.
ONLY ONE DRIVE WHEEL SLIPPING
Intervention-intervention times
For JTS versions:
Torque reduction by the engine management control unit through the alteration of the ignition advances, 6/100 of a second after the slipping limit is exceeded.
A further reduction in torque through a decrease in the throttle opening (by the engine management control unit through the motorized throttle body) after 15/100 of a second.
Intervention of the hydraulic system, a braking action exerted on the wheel that it slipping to guarantee a resistive force on the side with poor grip (T.C.). This resistive force allows the differential to transmit an equal torque with good grip.
For JTD versions:
Torque reduction via the engine control unit by reducing fuel flow, after 6/100 second.
Intervention of the hydraulic system, a braking action exerted on the wheel that it slipping to guarantee a resistive force on the side with poor grip (T.C.). This resistive force allows the differential to transmit an equal torque with good grip.
REGULATION OF ENGINE BRAKING TORQUE DURING OVER-RUN (MSR)
Vehicle instability during deceleration in poor grip conditions
The system recognizes this condition from the engine load, from the speed of the front and rear wheels and from the brake pedal sensor. In this case there is an increase in drive torque through the intervention of the engine management control unit opening the motorized throttle (petrol versions) or fuel flow (JTD versions) to overcome the natural instability of the vehicle due to the engine braking torque in poor grip conditions.
ASR CUT-OUT
If the A.S.R./M.S.R. is cut out, the following functions remain activated:
- ABS/EBD;
- T.C. up to a speed of 40 km
- VDC:
CUT-IN THRESHOLD
The different intervention levels between 2 and 6 km/h depend on environmental factors; some of the conditions have been described in the operating logics, others are:
- high acceleration level, high level thresholds;
- vehicle speed;
- tyre type (normal or winter). With winter tyres and good grip, high level thresholds; with winter tyres and low grip, thresholds are low. The system is capable of recognizing these conditions by comparing the acceleration of the drive wheels with the torque transmitted by the engine (engine load from the engine management control unit).
> Note: The ASR function is activated in all vehicle speed conditions, however, the intervention of the brakes is excluded above 40 km/h.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939002003.jpg]
VDC intervention display
The intervention of the VDC system is shown by the special warning light in the instrument panel flashing (5 Hz d.c. 50%).
> Note: the VDC system improves driving safety but there are limited situations which cannot be controlled by the VDC system, therefore it is not seen as a device which improves the performance of the vehicle but as a device that improves the safety of the vehicle.
DIAGNOSTIC FUNCTIONS
The ABS control unit is capable of carrying out the autodiagnosis of the system and, in the case of a fault, can:
- deactivate the entire system;
- partly deactivate the system.
|  | System status | ASR warning light in button | EBD warning light on NQS | ABS warning light on NQS | VDC warning light on NQS | HH warning light on NQS |

###### Operation of warning lights
The ABS control unit activates the warning lights according to the following logic:
- with the VDC on, the warning light in the panel is off and the warning light in the ASR button is off
- with ASR off, the VDC warning light on the control panel is off and the warning light on the ASR button is on;
- with the VDC activated, the warning light in the panel flashes and the warning light in the button is off
- when the VDC is faulty, the warning light on the control panel is on.
> Note: As the system is connected to the C-CAN line it has a diagnostic line known as line K. The diagnosis of the system can be carried out using the diagnostic equipment connected to the diagnostic socket.

###### Description of components
HYDRAULIC SYSTEM OPERATION
The electro-hydraulic unit on the version equipped with VDC has 4 additional solenoid valves.
When the (normally closed) intake solenoid valve is activated, the additional quantity of fluid required to increase the pressure and brake the wheel(s) can be received.
When the (normally open) solenoid valve is activated, the modulated pressure produced by the supply pump can be maintained in the circuit.
When the ESP system is not intervening, the electronic control unit:
- does not activate the (N.C.) intake solenoid valve (2).
- does not activate the (N.A.) operating solenoid valve (3).
In this way the system operates during the following stages:
- pressure increase;
- pressure maintenance;
- pressure reduction;
- pressure increase and resupply
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939002004.jpg]
During the intervention of the VDC system, the electronic control unit:
- activates the hydraulic pump (1)
- does not activate the (N.C.) intake solenoid valve (2).
- activates the (N.A.) operating solenoid valve (3).
Therefore the pressure produced by the pump (1) reaches the brake caliper and is modulated, on the request of the electronic control unit, by the discharge (5) and pressurizing (6) solenoid valves.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939002005.jpg]

#### DESCRIPTION OF COMPONENTS

##### Electrohydraulic unit
The electro-hydraulic unit consists of an electronic control unit and an electro-hydraulic control unit.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939002006.jpg]
1. Electronic control unit
2. Electrohydraulic control unit
3. Recovery pump assembly

###### Electronic control unit
The electronic control unit carries out the following functions:
- acquiring data coming from the wheel rpm sensors
- memorises the control parameters defined during the vehicle P.D.I.
- memorises the control software
- processes the data acquired
- controls the braking process
- detecting faults in the braking system components
- memorizing the fault codes and activating the ABS/EBD/ASR/VDC warning lights
- transmits and receives data via the diagnostic connector
- conversing with the engine management control unit
- controlling the ASR/MSR/VDC process;
- transmitting and receiving data via the C-CAN line.
PIN OUT
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939002007.jpg]
1 - CAN-L line
2 - CAN-H line
3 - ASR switch off
4 - ASR warning light off
5 - Not connected
6 - Diagnostics
7 - Right front sensor positive
8 - Right front sensor sensor negative
9 - Right rear sensor positive
10 - Right rear sensor negative
11 - Signal earth
12 - Supply

14 - CAN-H line

###### Hydraulic control unit
It performs the function of modulating the pressure of the fluid at the brake calipers via solenoid valves with the following operating stages:
- brake fluid pressure increase
- brake fluid pressure maintenance
- brake fluid pressure decrease.
> Note: The electro-hydraulic control unit is available from Parts filled with fluid; take care not to remove the protective caps or turn it upsidedown whilst moving it.
> Note: A sensor is fitted on the electro-hydraulic control unit for monitoring the pressure of the brake; this sensor is supplied together with the hydraulic unit so it cannot be replaced individually.
The electro-hydraulic control unit consists of:
- twelve 2-way solenoid valves
- a dual circuit scavenging pump
- two low pressure accumulators
- two high pressure accumulators
- brake fluid pressure sensor.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939002008.jpg]

###### Steering sensor
The steering angle sensor has the task of measuring the angles in degrees and the rotation speed of the steering wheel and making these figures available via the C-CAN (steering angle sensor node).
The sensor is built into the steering wheel stalk unit and cannot be dismantled individually.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939002009.jpg]
The sensor measures the following via internal electronics:
- angular position of the steering column;
- the rotation speed of the steering column.
This information is processed directly by the sensor and is made available at the brake node via the C-CAN.
The sensor has an angular measurement range of -720° - +720° and an angular resolution of 0.7°
The sensor must be zeroed in relation to the position of the steering wheel in order to work properly. This is carried out as follows:
- Turn the ignition key to the OFF position or remove;
- re-insert the key and start the engine;
- turn the steering wheel (even with the vehicle stationary) through 1/2 turn to the left;
- turn the steering wheel (even with the vehicle stationary) through 1/2 turn to the right;
- drive a short section in a straight line (wheels straight) for at least 100 metres and at a speed over 8 km until the warning light goes off.
The sensor has an autodiagnostic function and is capable of carrying out a check on the plausibility of the information processed.

###### Lateral yaw/acceleration sensor
The two yaw and lateral acceleration sensors are designed to measure rotation of the vehicle on the vertical axis (yaw) and lateral acceleration.
Connection to the ABS control unit is via the CAN line.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939002010.jpg]
The sensor has the following functional specifications:
Supply voltage:
- minimum value 6.0 V
- maximum value 21.5 V
- nominal value 12 V
Operating temperature:
- Minimum value -40°C
- Maximum value +85°C
Current uptake at 12 V:
- nominal value 50 mA
Lateral acceleration sensor:
- Measurement range ± 1.5 g
The sensor consists of a plastic casing that houses the sensitive elements which detect slewing and lateral acceleration and the electronic management.
The sensor has a connector with six pins all of which are connected.
The sensor is located at the centre of gravity, on the tunnel between the two front seats.
The sensor receives a direct power supply from the battery and, simultaneously, provides the yaw and acceleration signal to the ABS control unit via the CAN line.

###### Active sensors
The adoption of active sensors offers the following advantages:
- less sensitivity to the distance between the sensor and the magnetic ring (gap)
- a reduction in sensitivity to electro-magnetic interference
- a saving in weight and size;
- a simplification of the transmission couplings through the elimination of the phonic wheels.
Active sensors consist of two fundamental components:
- a multipolar magnetic coder (1) built into the bearing of the wheel hub bearing with controls
- a magnetoresistance receiver (2) facing the codifier.
FRONT SENSORS
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939002011.jpg]
REAR SENSORS
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939002012.jpg]
The active sensor operates according to the variation in the internal electrical resistance according to the intensity and direction of the lines of force of an external magnetic field (multipolar magnetic codifier) producing a variable square wave signal whose frequency varies according to the rotation speed of the wheel, but with a constant amplitude.
The active sensor is therefore an integrated electronic sensor, connected by means of a cable to the ABS control unit, from which it receives an electrical supply and to which it transmits the speed of the vehicle.
The flywheel is a multipolar ring, an elastomer with a certain quantity of magnetic particles which, by means of a special magnetization technique, are orientated to produce different magnets with alternate North South poles in a circumference arrangement.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939002013.jpg]

###### Asr on/off button
It has the task of switching the ASR/MSR system off and has an LED.
Button 1) is integral with the central console.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939002014.jpg]

## GENERAL REMARKS - STEERING  [939005118]
- Path: Descriptions > 41 STEERING UNIT > GENERAL REMARKS - STEERING
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939005118

#### SPECIFICATIONS
The steering control has been designed to guarantee the best performance for the driver during sporty driving together with excellent handling and limited effort during parking manoeuvres.
The development of these objectives, in conjunction with the search for excellent driving comfort, has led to the production of a steering system with the following technical specifications:
- steering wheel turns: 2.33 in total on all versions
- steering ratio: 13.0 steering wheel turns/wheel rotation
- steering wheel effort: ~ 4 Nm when steering from stationary
- turning circle: 11.1 m
Driving comfort has been improved by taking care of the power assisted steering system sound insulation and by adopting a new design steering wheel and steering column featuring high structural strength. In addition, a new type vibrational damper with excellent uncoupling has been fitted on the intermediate steering column shaft.
Lastly, great attention has been paid to passive safety both in terms of the layout, with the movement of the electric steering lock to the front area of the steering column, away from the area of the knees, and with the adoption of a controlled energy absorption collapsing device on the steering column. This, in conjunction with the steering wheel and knee air bags and the retaining belts, makes it possible to produce a five star performance in EUNCAP impact tests.

#### HYDRAULIC SYSTEM For 4 x 2 version
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939002015.jpg]
1. Power assisted steering pump
2. Power steering fluid reservoir
3. Steering box
4. Cooling coil
The hydraulic circuit has a hydraulic pump rotated by service belts; the pump draws in oil from the reservoir near the actual pump; the pump supply reaches the steering box; the fluid leaving the steering box is sent to the reservoir passing through the cooling coil at the side of the radiator.

#### HYDRAULIC SYSTEM For 4 x 4 version
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/946001133.jpg]
1. Power assisted steering pump
2. Power steering fluid reservoir
3. Steering box
4. Heat exchanger
The hydraulic circuit has a hydraulic pump rotated by service belts; the pump draws in oil from the reservoir near the actual pump; the pump supply reaches the steering box; the fluid leaving the steering box is sent to the reservoir passing through a heat exchanger first.

#### STEERING BOX
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939002016.jpg]
Designed according to the constant ratio rack and pinion model, the size guarantees a max force of 10.85 KN power assistance.
The mounting supports for the box on the lower frame are designed to break in the case of a crash to maximize the energy absorbed by the bodyshell.

#### STEERING COLUMN
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939002017.jpg]
1. Locking lever
2. Electric steering lock
3. Lower cover
4. Mounting bracket on dashboard crossmember
Designed in accordance with the telescopic covers, it guarantees:
- vertical adjustment with ± 2 degrees travel,
- axial adjustment with 45 mm of total travel.
The locking lever is located under the upper cover, in the special housing for the lower cover, in accordance with the most up to date EUNCAP safety requirements.
The electric steering lock, fitted as standard, is housed on the lower steering column cover, by the mounting bracket on the dashboard crossmember.
This means that it is out of the way of the driver's knees in line with current EUNCAP recommendations. In line with current European legislation, the steering lock guarantees the locking of the steering wheel by means of a special Rencol clutch bush which allows rotation for torques between 100-240 Nm to prevent damaing the mechanical steering components if there is a theft attempt.
The steering column has a controlled energy absorption collapsing device which allows axial travel of 45 mm in addition to the adjustment travel.

## INTRODUCTION - SUSPENSION AND WHEELS  [939003524]
- Path: Descriptions > 44 SUSPENSION AND WHEELS > INTRODUCTION - SUSPENSION AND WHEELS
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939003524

#### CONSTRUCTION SPECIFICATIONS
Front suspension with quadrilateral, i.e. two superimposed triangles. In this configuration the shock absorber and the spring are flexible damping elements without structural functions.
The rear suspension is the multilink type designed to allow:
- recovery of camber during roll to keep the tyre vertical in order to maximize the lateral force that can be transmitted;
- the elastokinmeatic retraction of the wheel centre when going over an obstacle to reduce the longitudinal component of the impact force;
- control of steering round bends and when braking through a stabilizing effect and prompt response in the various usage conditions.
The combination of the two suspensions makes it possible to produce the following strong points:
- precise, gradual steering and steering wheel load
- good responsiveness
- good stability and ease of control even in poor grip conditions
- very smooth, balanced movements
- very good comfort for a sports vehicle.
Front and rear wheel hubs with integrated bearing for A.B.S. active sensors.

#### FRONT SUSPENSION
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939002018.jpg]
The quadrilateral structure guarantees very good dynamic performance, excellent steering and precise driving.
The track rod end-steering knuckle connection has been retracted and moved towards the outside. This has made it possible to improve the stability of the vehicle during braking.
Careful attention to the matching of the steering geometry and wheel arch volume has made it possible to produce high steering angles even with larger tyres with notable improvements in the turning circle.

##### Front suspension components
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939002019.jpg]
1. Wheel damper
2. Spring-shock absrober assembly
3. Lower track control arm
4. Rear bush
5. Upper track control arm
6. Sliding bushes
7. Chassis
8. Wheel hub
9. Anti-roll bar
The wheel damper has been redesigned at the points where it is connected to the levers using the space available inside the 16" wheel rims to the fullest with considerable benefits in terms of lateral strength.
The coaxial spring-shock absorber assembly with bi-tube shock absorber has been increased in size and now has a 15 mm stem with a 32 mm valve assembly. These increased dimensions have improved the filtering capacity of the shock absorber also reducing hysteresis levels. The connection to the bodyshell takes place by means of a large split mounting with a high noise filtering capacity.
The aluminium lower track control arm combines excellent structural specifications with being lighter than previous solutions. The main feature is the bushes connected to the chassis. The front bush, which is extremely rigid, supports most of the side and longitudinal loads opposing lateral deformation with benefits in terms of loss of camber when cornering. The hydraulic rear bush has doubled in size and increases the harshness longitudinal filtering capacity.
The upper aluminium suspension arm has a pair of sliding bushes, the preferred solution because it is the best in terms of smooth steering. The dry friction bushes are tougher and more reliable. The mounting points on the bodyshell have vertical reinforcements and have been designed for maximum structural rigidity improving the noise filtering capacity.
The suspension has been secured to the bodyshell by means of a closed geometry frame with high lateral rigidity. In addition to the ten fastenings on the bodyshell there is also a strut between the chassis and the bodyshell side members which makes it possible to control the collapsing of the front section during a crash in conjunction with the suspension frame.

#### REAR SUSPENSION
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939002020.jpg]
The multilink structure suspension makes it possible to control the movements of the wheels resulting in the highest level performance compromises. In this case the three lever solution with a transverse plate has made it possible to improve the performance of the various longitudinal components and achieve better filtering of lateral harshness resulting in a fast response time and improved stability and road holding.

##### Rear suspension components
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939002021.jpg]
1. Longitudinal bar
2. Hydraulic bush
3. Steering knuckle
4. Spring-shock absrober assembly
5. Camber arm
6. Crossmember
7. Anti-roll bar
8. Wheel hub
The high resistance steel longitudinal arm has the task of guiding the damper during jolts guaranteeing longitidunal motion at the same time. Fitted with a hydraulic bush 80 mm in diameter, it allows soft retractions with excellent damping levels for post-impact consequences. The fltering bush is secured to the bodyshell by means of a bracket with three fastenings. The fastening has been improved by placing the retainer inside the bodyshell. This has made it possible to achieve good strength properties and improved pitch variation with further benefits when driving over obstacles.
In addition to having a high strength hub, the aluminium stub axle also houses the connecting bushes for the camber lever and for the longitudinal arm.
The latter is connected by a rigid rubber-metal bush matched with a uniball joint with a teflon coating. Thanks to this and the front bush it has been possible to achieve a fast response together with excellent road holding thanks also to the considerable toe in of the wheels under lateral loads.
The stub axle is compatible for 4x4 applications.
The bi-tube shock absorbers with coaxial springs make it possible to control the three damping areas with precision both when compressed and recoiled, thereby producing a good compromise between handling and comfort.
The spring shock absorber assembly is secured to the bodyshell by means of a large split shock absorber mounting which has made it possible to produce an excellent filtering performance even with high damping forces.
The camber arm, in addition to allowing the adjustment of static camber, has made it possible to produce a geometry that guarantees excellent recovery of camber during jolts in order to always ensure the best impression on the ground for the tyre even when driving at the limit.
The entire suspension is connected to the vehicle by means of a high resistance steel crossmember, insulated from the bodyshell by means of four 90 mm bushes that increase the insulation of high frequencies. All the suspension mounting points have been designed to be as strong as possible resulting in fast response times and improved filtering with a reduction in bodyshell entry noise.

## 5040 AIR CONDITIONING CASING AND COMPONENTS  [939003527]
- Path: Descriptions > 50 AUXILIARY UNITS > 5040 AIR CONDITIONING CASING AND COMPONENTS
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939003527

#### INTRODUCTION
The climate control system makes it possible to alter the features of the air introduced into the passenger compartment (temperature, humidity) designed to create and maintain a high level of comfort whilst driving.

##### Climate control system components
The climate control system components are illustrated in the diagram.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939003833.jpg]
1. Linear pressure switch
2. Condenser
3. Drier filter built into the condenser
4. Low pressure gas pipe
5. Expansion valve
6. Evaporator
7. Dect/distributor assembly
8. Control panel with electronic control unit
9. Rear control panel (triple zone version)
10. Compressor
11. High pressure gas pipe
12. High pressure fluid pipe

##### Operating principle
The aim of refrigeration equipment is to absorb heat from an environment. In order to do this an air conditioner has recourse to certain fluids (known as refrigerants) capable of cooling down (lowering their temperature) and changing state (from liquid to gas) when they are subject to a large drop in pressure, expanding. They are therefore capable of absorbing heat from the environment. When the temperature increases thereby also increasing the pressure, they change state, another time, from gas to liquid, and condense.
The first problem is therefore to liquefy this gas which can be achieved simply by bringing it to a temperature below that of evaporation (or boiling) which, as has already been stated, is -26°C at atmospheric pressure for R134a.
In order for this to be achieved at ambient temperature which, in our case, may be rather high (in the engine compartment), it is necessary to increase the evaporation point of the gas so that it remains liquid until the moment it is made to expand to produce the desired refrigerant effect.
To raise the boiling point of the gas its pressure must be increased, at the same time, decreasing the temperature.
In order for this to take place the system requires a certain amount of power. This power, supplied by the compressor, is subtracted from the power produced by the engine.
The operating principle of the refrigerant cycle phases in the air conditioning system for a motor vehicle can be summed up as follows.
The gaseous R134a refrigerant is drawn in by the compressor at a pressure of between 0.5 and 2 bar and is compressed at a value of between 10 and 17 bar. The boiling point at these pressures is around 60 °C.
This fluid, heated by the compression stage at 80 - 100 °C, always in a gaseous state, in the compressor where, through the effect of the cooling air flow (produced by the vehicle moving forward or through the action of the fan) that passes through, reaches condensation point, changing at high pressure to a liquid state.
Later on the refrigerant passes through a filter which has three functions: to trap the impurities, absorb the dampness contained in the circuit and work as a reserve reservoir for the actual refrigerant.
The refrigerant reaches the expansion valve, where it is introduced into the evaporator where the pressure is around 1.5 atm. (1.52 bar). At this pressure the liquid/vapour system saturated with the refrigerant fluid is in equilibrium at a temperature of about -7 °C. At the same time, the air that passes through the evaporator (through the action of a fan), being at a considerably higher temperature than the refrigerant fluid it contains, causes it to boil and evaporate completely by imparting heat. On cooling, the air deposits some of the dampness it contains on the evaporator fins in the form of droplets which are collected in a chamber and drained off from the vehicle.
The cooled and dehumidified air is sent inside the vehicle. The refrigerant is drawn in by the compressor again at the evaporator outlet, thereby giving rise to a new cycle once again.
The route of the refrigerant fluid can be summarized as follows:
- In the compressor - the fluid coming from the evaporator is gaseous (temp. -5, -7°C, pressure 0.5 - 2 bar). Compression phase - the gaseous fluid is overheated (temp. 80 -100 °C, pressure 10 -17 bar).
- Condensator - Compression phase: the fluid gives off heat to the outside, cools down and returns to a liquid state (temp. 40 -60°C, pressure 10 -17 bar).
- Thermostatic expansion valve - Expansion phse - the fluid loses pressure (0.5 - 2 bar, possibly even 3 bar) becomes a gas + liquid mixture; the temperature is low, typical of air conditioning.
- Evaporator - Evaporation phase - the fluid becomes completely gaseous because the hot air driven by the fan finds itself at a higher temperature than the refrigerant fluid and causes it to boil and evaporate completely giving off heat. The temperature is low, typical of air conditioning (pressure 0.5 - 2 bar).

##### Types of system
This vehicle can be equipped with different climate control systems for the passenger compartment:
- manual climate control
- dual zone automatic climate control
- triple zone automatic climate control
Manual climate control: the user sets the air temperature, distribution and flow rate and they remain like that until they are altered by the user later on.
Automatic climate control (dual/triple zone): the user can set the parameters and select automatic system management. If they so wish, the user can preseve the facility to manage the system manually.
In addition, the automatic climate control system on this vehicle is the dual zone type (driver's zone and front passenger zone) or triple zone (driver's zone, front passenger zone and rear seat zone), in other words the system has dual controls for the driver and the passenger and is capable of managing the settings for the two users separately, varying the air temperature and distribution parameters (the flow rate cannot be different in the zones) with a certain degree of independence.

#### MANUAL CLIMATE CONTROL
The manual climate control system control panel is illustrated in the diagram below.

6. Interior air recirculation on/off button
7. Climate control compressor on/off button
The manually operated climate control system is managed by an electronic controlunit, known as the Climate Control Node (NCL) connected to the vehicle electrical system B-CAN and incorporated in the climate control system control panel in the middle of the dashboard.

##### Operating strategy
The manual air conditioning also allows the user to manage the temperature and the intake of air into the passenger compartment using the control knobs and buttons.
The following parameters/functions can be altered manually:
- Temperature
- Distribution in 5 positions
- Fan speed.
- Compressor enablement
- Defrosting/demisting function
- Recirculation
The transmission of the air mixing, air distribution and recirculation commands from the knobs to the climate control casing takes place by means of electric motors.
The compressor can only be activated if one of the fan speeds is switched on.

#### AUTOMATIC CLIMATE CONTROL
The automatic climate control system is managed by a control unit which is capable, thanks to an extremely sophisticated operating logic, of controlling the temperature in two zones of the passenger compartment heating or cooling the air to produce the desired comfort level.
The climate control system automatically adjusts the following parameters/functions:
- Air temperature at the driver's/passenger side vents
- Fan speed (continuous variation)
- Driver/passenger side air distribution
- Engagement of compressor
- Recirculation

##### Controls
The user interface for this control unit has the following layout.

###### Dual/triple zone front controls
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939003835.jpg]
1. Air distribution selection buttons (driver side and passenger side)
2. Driver's temperature adjustment knob
3. AUTO function activation button (automatic operation)
4. Climate control system information display
5. Passenger side temperature adjustment knob
6. Heated rear windscreen on/off button
7. MAX DEF function activation button (rapid defrosting/demisting of front windows, heated rear windscreen and exterior rear view mirrors)
8. Fan speed increase/decrease buttons
9. MONO function activation button (temperature setting alignment)
10. Interior air recirculation on/off button
11. Climate control compressor on/off button
12. Interior air temperature sensor

###### Triple zone rear controls
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939003836.jpg]
1. AUTO function activation button (automatic operation) and closing of air flow to rear seats
2. Rear temperature adjustment knob
3. Air distribution selection buttons
4. Rear temperature display
The following parameters/functions can be set/altered manually:
- Temperature requested
- Fan speed
- Distribution in 7 positions
- Compressor enabling/disabling
- Defrosting/demisting function
- Recirculation
- Single zone function
Manual selections always take priority over automatic ones, except those related to the safety of the vehicle, and are memorized until the user switches back to automatic operation.
The manual setting of a function does not adeversely affect the control of the others set automatically, in particular the control of the temperature is always automatic when the system is working with the exception of situations in which the manual selections adversely affect the possibility of controlling/maintaining the required temperature; in this case the temperatures shown on the display flash indicating that the temperature is no longer under the control of the automatic system.
Each time it is switched on (Key on) the system restores the conditions memorized when it was switched off, with the exception of the MAX-DEF function which is zeroed.
There is a facility for switching the system off manually (OFF) using the fan button until 0 bars are selected for the flow rate, completely deactivating the air conditioning system (except for Recirculation and Heated Rear Windscreen) and isolating the passenger compartment from the outside environment.
The MAX-DEF function groups together a collection of actions that make it possible to quickly demist the windscreen, the side windows, the heataed rear windscreen and the exterior rear view mirrors.

###### Climate control system control unit
The climate control system is managed automatically by an electronic control unit known as the Climate Control Node (NCL) which is charged with keeping the air climate control conditions set, and therefore desired, by the user (or users) unchanged.
The NCL is connected to the vehicle's electrical system B-CAN.
The NCL is incorporated in the climate control system control panel fitted in the centre of the dashboard. The rear view of the control unit is shown in the diagram with the connection to the electrical system highlighted and the connector pin out listed below.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939003837.jpg]

If the control unit is being replaced, the Parts Dept. will send a pristine component: once fitted, the data memorized in the Body Computer must be transferred to it by carrying out the "PROXI ALIGNMENT" procedure using the Examiner.
> Note: The various actuators in the climate control system unit, even if similar, are specifically programmed and are not interchangeable.

##### Operating strategy
The principle on which the temperature control is based is linked to the "EQUIVALENT TEMPERATURE" concept.
A control based on the equivalent temperature concept does not try and keep the passenger compartment at a constant temperature, but tries to maintain the user's feeling of heat.
The thermal sensation depends on all the thermal energy exchanges with the environment and is estimated by the climate control system control unit on the basis of ambient parameters.
In particular, inside a VEHICLE, it depends on the following:
- Average temperature in the passenger compartment
- Temperature of the air sent to the passenger compartment interior
- Temperature of the walls and surfaces exposed to passengers (dashboard, seats, etc.)
- Air flow rate in the passenger compartment
- Sun's rays
There is a sensor to measure the sun's rays, which acquires a bilateral signal (left-right) which contributes towards determining the comfort conditions in terms of air distribution and temperature.
The only action that the user has to take is to identify and select an equivalent temperature value that is comfortable for them and, irrespective of outside conditions, the system will work to adjust all the variables under its control to ensure the desired thermal sensation.
The system automatically adjusts the following parameters/functions:
- air temperature at the vents
- air distribution
- air flow rate in the passenger compartment
- compressor enablement
- recirculation
All these functions can be modified manually, in other words the user can intervene and select one or more functions at will: in this way the user removes the control of the functions selected manually from the automatic system (with the system unable to intervene unless it is for safety reasons) to guarantee the requested equivalent temperature.

###### Air mixture control
The control of the outlet air temperature at the vents is fairly important in the adaptation of the Equivalent Temperature to the value set with reference to comfort conditions.
This check is carried out by activating the mixture flap.
The movement of the mixture actuator is filtered so that movements that are too quick cannot take place thereby preventing unpleasant fluctuations in temperature.

###### Air flow rate control
Another fundamental parameter for reaching and maintaing the Equivalent Temperature at the value set is the control of the outlet air flow rate at the vents. This check is carried out by activating the fan speed control.
For this purpose the control algorithm calculates a flow rate figure dependent on the previous flow rate and the difference between the objective equivalent temperature and the one measured.
Similarly to the calculation of the Mixture, in this case too the value of the flow rate is filtered so that variations that are too rapid are not produced; a "seasonal" parameter is also taken into consideration to adapt the operation of the fan depending on whether it is summer or winter.

##### Use of the system
As described previously, the climate control system control system is based on the equivalent temperature and works to stabilize the thermal sensation inside the passenger compartment (compensating for any variation in the outside climate conditions).
The user has to identify and select an equivalent temperature value that they are comfortable with and, irrespective of outside conditions (it does not matter whether it is summer or winter, sunny or raining), the system will work, adjusting all the variables in its power to ensure the desired thermal sensation.
- To check that the system control is fully prepared for automatic operation, make sure that the words FULL AUTO are shown on the display.
To produce the fully automatic conditions, press the AUTO buttons which enable the automatic adjustment functions: DISTRIBUTION, AIR FLOW RATE, COMPRESSOR ENABLEMENT, RECIRCULATION MANAGEMENT.
If the air flow rate or distribution is selected manually, the word FULL will disappear; if the compressor is disabled manually the LED will go out: if the system is capable, depending on the ambient temperature, of keeping the comfort level constant, the word AUTO will remain on, otherwise it will go out.
- The compressor button enables the COMPRESSOR ON/OFF function When the compressor is working, the user is guaranteed not only the possibility of cooling the temperature of the passenger compartment (especially in hot weather), but also the chance of dehumidifying the air (preventing the problem of the windows misting up, especially in cold weather).
The compressor, however, cannot work when the outside temperature is low. In this case, to prevent problems of misting up, the system forces the dynamic air intake leaving the button enabled (this way the user can set it how they want).
In any case, if there visibility problems linked to the windscreen misting up, it is a good idea to check that the recirculation button LED is off.
The recirculation button can be managed manually or automatically. Automatic management of the recirculation is also connected (if present) to the air quality sensor (AQS) which, on recognizing the pollutant factors present inthe air, closes the recirculation automatically.
If there is no AQS, the automatic management of the recirculation is carried out with a view to improving the thermal adjustment transitions.
The exchange of air inside the passenger compartment is also guaranteed (every 25 minutes consecutively with the recirculation on, the system moves automatically to outside air for a period of 60 seconds).
When the AQS sensor is present, it is disabled automatically at low outside temperatures to prevent the windscreen from misting up. The user, using the rolling recirculation button, can, on exiting from the fully automatic function, re-enable the operation of the AQS sensor.
> Note: The information transmitted by the AQS is compared by the system with the information from the (optional) DEFOG sensor (which controls the degree of humidity present on the windscreen). If the windscreen is misted up and the compressor is disabled, the system forces the recirculation open for safety reasons (the priority of the system is obviously to ensure good visibility for the driver).
To switch the system off, keep the speed rocker switch pressed at the "-" symbol until the word OFF appears on the display.
When the system is OFF, the passenger compartment is insulated from the outside (recirculation closed, LED in the button on). The recirculation can, however, be opened (to allow outside air to enter the passenger compartment) by pressing the recirculation button (switching off the LED).
The system contains pre-defined functions that determine specific operation in certain conditions.
- LO function. When a temperature of less than 16°C is set, the "maximum cooling" condition is produced; in these circumstances the system is in MONO operation, the words FULL and AUTO go out and the following actions are activated: temperature regulator in maximum cold position, front air distribution, air flow rate at seasonal maximum, compressor enablement, recirculation as requested by user.
- HI function. When a temperature of more than 32°C is set, the "maximum heating" condition is produced; in these circumstances the system is in MONO operation, the words FULL and AUTO go out and the following actions are activated: temperature regulator in maximum hot position, air distribution to feet, air flow rate at seasonal maximum, compressor managed according to logic (depending on whether rest is more than 2°C), recirculation as requested by user.
- MAX DEF function. When the specific button (7) is pressed, the system switches to MONO, the words FULL and AUTO go out and the following actions are implemented: temperature regulator in maximum hot position, air distribution to the windscreen, increase in the air flow rate (if the temperature of the engine is sufficiently high), compressor function enabled (LED on), recirculation forced open, HEATED REAR WINDSCREEN activated (LED on).

##### Functions

###### Temperature setting control knob
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939003838.jpg]
Knob for setting passenger compartment temperature (zone by zone).
By turning the knob for the desired zone (driver/passengers) the desired passenger compartment temperature can be increased (clockwise direction) or decreased (anti-clockwise direction).
The increases/decreases are in steps of 0.5 ºC and one complete revolution of the knob produces 24 steps.
The temperature settings are memorized at the key off and then restored at the next key on.
The temperature range can be set between 16 and 32 ºC; below 16 ºC the value set becomes «LO» whilst above 32 ºC the value set becomes «HI».
If the user sets a temperature below the outside temperature, with the compressor button disabled, the system is not capable of reaching it or maintaining it and this impossibility is signalled by the Temperature setting flashing.

###### Hi condition
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939003839.jpg]
The HI condition is reached by setting a temperature above 32 ºC.
This request by the user switches off the words FULL and AUTO, forces the system to MONO and involves the following actions:
- Mixer in fully hot position.
- Distribution towards the feet.
- Air flow rate increase (if the temperature of the engine is sufficiently high).
- Recirculation remains as requested by user.
Manual settings are allowed in the HI condition.
Exiting the MONO condition using the button determines exiting the HI function and the temperature setting of 32° C for both zones.
If the driver turns the temperature setting this moves the passenger setting out of HI to 32° C
If the passenger turns the temperature setting this also moves the driver's setting out of HI (to 32ºC), then changing their own settings placing the system in the 2/3 zone mode.

###### Lo condition
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939003840.jpg]
The LO condition is reached by setting a temperature below 16 ºC.
This request by the user switches off the words FULL and AUTO, forces the system to MONO and involves the following actions:
- Mixer in max cold position.
- Air distribution to the dashboard
- Air flow rate increase
- Compressor enablement
Manual settings are allowed in the LO condition.
Exiting the MONO condition using the button determines exiting the LO function and the temperature setting of 16° C for both zones.
If the driver turns the temperature setting this moves the passenger setting out of LO to 16° C
If the passenger turns the temperature setting this also moves the driver's setting out of LO (to 16ºC), then changing their own settings placing the system in the Dual Zone mode.
The flashing logic is valid, if the compressor is disabled after the LO request and the forced recirculation is automatic if it was not already.

###### Auto button
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939003841.jpg]
Pressing this button restores the automatic operation of the following functions
- Air distribution
- Fan speed
- Compressor
- Recirculation
The words FULL AUTO lit up indicate that all the above mentioned functions are controlled automatically.
The word FULL goes out in the area considered when a Distribution manoeuvre is carried out manually.
The word FULL goes out in all the zones when a manual operation is carried out on the flow rate, compressor or recirculation.
The word AUTO also goes out if the control system (mainly when the compressor is manually disabled) does not reach or maintain the required temperature.
The button that disables the Compressor does not switch off the word AUTO when the system is capable of maintaining the desired comfort.

###### Distribution buttons
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939003842.jpg]
There are 7 possible positions for the air distribution (VENT, BI-LEVEL, HEAT, FLOOR, DEF, HI-LEVEL, TRI-LEVEL).
In Automatic mode the system manages the distribution and does not display its selection.
One of the 7 positions can be selected manually by activating the buttons according to the following combination logic:
- Main Distributions:
DEF
VENT
FLOOR
- Combined Distributions
BI-LEVEL
HEAT
HI-LEVEL
TRI-LEVEL
With the combined distribution activated, the LED goes out when one of the two buttons is pressed.
With the main distribution activated (one LED on), when the same button is pressed the existing distribution is confirmed.

###### Recirculation
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939003843.jpg]
The recirculation button operates with a ROLLING logic.
By pressing the AUTO button, automatic management of the recirculation is selected
- Automatic
The A in the button lights up
This informs the user that the recirculation is managed automatically to improve the thermodynamic comfort; in addition, if an AQS sensor is fitted, it is also dependent on the quality of the air.
> Note: For safety reasons (e.g. windows misted up, long periods of closure), A is switched off to signal the deactivation of the automatic control.
When A is switched off, it is possible to select automatic operation using the recirculation rolling button and exiting from the system fully automatic mode.
- Recirculation forced closed
With this type of manual operation, the red LED signals the closure of the recirculation flap.
- Recirculation forced open (outside air)
With this type of manual operation, the red LED off signals the forced opening of the outside air flap.
> Note: This mode should be selected if the windows are misted up.

###### Air flow rate variation control
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939003844.jpg]
The air flow rate can be adjusted manually in steps, which are displayed as one bar for every 2 steps up to a maximum of 6 bars when it then goes out.
If there have been no manual interventions, the fan speed is controlled continuously by the system and this is shown on the display by the relevant number of bars lighting up according to the flow rate.
If the ventilation control is operated manually, the FULL AUTO condition is exited. In particular, to increase or decrease the fan speed, press the rocker switch on the + and - symbols.
At the key on, if the control unit is controlling the air flow rate Automatically, this air flow rate corresponds to the 1st bar (minimum flow rate) until the engine is started.
If the compressor is disabled, the ventilation control can be operated manually until the display shows 0 bar.
If the compressor is enabled and the engine started, the manual ventilation cannot go below 1 bar on the display because with the compressor enabled there must be a minimum air flow rate to prevent ice from forming in the evaporator.

###### Switching off the control unit (off)
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939003845.jpg]
Operating the air flow rate control (decrease) below 0 bars (fan off) causes the word OFF only to light up on the display.
The following actions take place in OFF:
- memorizing of the current state
- switching off of the display (with the exception of the OFF symbol)
- closed recirculation and relevant LED lit up
- compressor excluded
- fan excluded
- mixer in max cold position
- distribution in Vent
- in the OFF state the Heated Rear Windscreen button is managed normally without activating the climate control system.
In the OFF condition the recirculation button is dual control (ON/OFF) opening (red LED off) and closing (red LED on) the flap, without managing the automatic operation (red LED off).
Pressing the air flow rate control button at the + symbol or pressing any button (except for the Heated Rear Windscreen and Recirculation) or pressing any of the AUOT buttons, switches the system back on.
When exiting from OFF, the recirculation returns to Automatic mode.
Pressing the OFF button on the rear control makes the word OFF disappear in the display and the air flow to the rear seats stops.

###### Compressor enablement
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939003846.jpg]
With the compressor enablement LED on, pressing the button switches the LED off and disables the compressor
Once the button has been pressed, this selection remains memorized indefinitely even after the vehicle has been switched off, the same as for the other manual controls.
The button is dual function: pressing it a second time re-enables the compressor and switches the LED on.
With the compressor disabled, the system checks whether the outside temperature is higher or lower than/the same as the temperature set:
- if the outside temperature is less than the temperature set then the system works normally and is capable of complying with the request even without the compressor being switched on;
- of the outside temperature is higher than the temperature set then the system is not capable of complying with the request and signals this by making the temperature settings flash.
The control (system with compressor disabled and outside temperature higher than temperature set) is activated at the key on.

###### Mono
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939003847.jpg]
Pressing the MONO button determines the following action:
- the temperature set on the front and rear passenger displays is made the same as that set by the driver and the LED comes on.
From that moment the system behaves like a single zone system.
Pressing the MONO button again or altering the temperature set by the front and rear passengers causes the following results:
- the MONO button LED goes out and there is a shift to dual/triple zone temperature control.

###### Max def
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939003848.jpg]
The Max-Def function is also managed with the engine switched off.
The following operations are activated:
- Max-Def LED lit up
- memorizing of the function state and previous displays of Max-Def control
- words FULL and AUTO switched off and automatic recirculation (if on)
- switching on of the DEF distribution, compressor enablement, MONO and HEATED REAR WINDSCREEN LEDs
- display of fully hot temperature (HI)
- display of the ventilation in the front display
- switching off of the rear panel
- activation of the following controls
- air flow rate increase (with coolant temperature sufficiently hot)
- air distribution in Def position (before implementing the mix)
- forced air intake open (dynamic)
- compressor function enabled
- AQS disabled (if present)
- rear windscreen defrosting
> Note: When exiting from Max-Def the mix is implemented first and then the distribution.
During the operation of the Max-Def it is possible to:
- Alter the air flow rate (up/down) at will
- Deactivate the heated rear windscreen
It is not possible to
- Alter the temperature setting (driver/passengers)
- Alter the distribution setting
It is possible to interrupt the Max-Def function by activating any one of the climate control buttons (Recirculation, Compressor, AUTO, MONO, Max-Def) implementing the return to the prior to the Max-Def plus the implementation of the control for the button pressed.

###### Heated rear windscreen
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939003849.jpg]
The defrosting of the rearscreen is activated both through the special button and through the Max-Def procedure. The display of the function status takes place through the LED switching on/off.
The function requesting the activation of the heated rear windscreen is only subject to the key-on condition.
