Cancelling the procedure
If the rear fog lamp key is not pressed within 10s while entering the operating mode, the procedure is aborted: in this case, the siren emits 5 beeps to notify the operator and the BC maintains the previous operating mode valid.
The market may be changed from 1,2,3,4,5 using a diagnostic tester or manual procedure.
It is not possible to enable/disable the market by entering 0.

###### Diagnosing external modules
The BC diagnoses the operation of the serial line for connection to the siren and external modules, checking for short circuits to earth, to the battery and for the presence of open circuits.
A diagnostic check is carried out on the serial line when communication is activated, typically upon activation of the alarm system.
The external modules are diagnosed when the system is activated by diagnostic commands from which the following information is obtained.
No diagnostic checks are required for the perimeter protection switches.
The diagnostic information obtained at the time of activation is stored in the EEPROM to ensure the system can be serviced.
To carry out fault diagnosis, use the diagnostic equipment provided.

###### Active diagnosis
During a diagnostic session, the BC may be required to carry out a diagnostic check on the external modules: the BC then sends the appropriate command and communicates the outcome to the diagnostic instrument.
If the BC cannot communicate with the module during this operation, the response to the diagnostic instrument will be:
- serial line interference
- module not responding.
Similarly, a diagnostic check may be requested on the serial line, with the following possible outcomes. OK, short circuit to earth, short circuit to battery.
It is also possible to read the alarm cause table stored in the BC.

###### Recovery
If an external module (ultrasound, tilt) is recognized as not functioning, it is excluded for the entire surveillance cycle.
The next time the system is switched on, the diagnostic check is carried out again on the modules which should be reactivated if they are recognized as working.

##### Components

###### Anti-theft device siren
The following figure shows the antitheft siren.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939000068.jpg]
The main specifications of the siren are:
- sealed casing;
- green batteries for self-powering once the cables have been cut;
- battery recharging from control;
- programmable acoustic emission type;
- serial communication with the body computer and other alarm system components;
- self-diagnostics.
The siren (Stand –alone) is connected to the rest of the system with:
- a dedicated serial line between the NBC and siren;
- power supply for the siren/internal battery recharging.
The siren can respond to diagnostic messages sent by the NBC (internal self-diagnosis).
The siren is located in the left front wheel arch.
SIREN PINOUT
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939000069.jpg]
1 - Siren power supply
2 - Serial line
3 - Earth
4 - N.C.

###### Volumetric / tilt sensors
The volumetric and tilt sensors are fitted in the passenger compartment on the courtesy light.
The volumetric sensors consist of a receiver and an ultrasound receiver fitted in a module connected to the antitheft control unit.
The tilt sensor detects angular changes compared to the vehicle's longitudinal axis and transverse axis.
Both sensors may be deactivated (both together and not separately) by means of the appropriate button.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939000070.jpg]
1 - Sensor deactivation led
2 - Sensor deactivation button
3 - Ultrasound volumetric sensors
4 - Tilt sensor (inside courtesy light)

###### Receiver
SPECIFICATIONS
The remote control/receiver system interfaces with the NBC to activate the following functions:
- activate central opening/locking of the doors and, where specified, of the windows, sun-roof and courtesy light activation.
- turn the alarm system on and off.
The remote control system consists of:
- sending unit: this is fitted in the TEG, is radio controlled and sends a rolling code to the receiver. It has tow or three function control keys and a LED to verify code transmission and battery charge status.
- receiver: radio-controlled, built into the NBC with operating frequency of 433.92 Mhz.
The receiver is located in the NBC and equipped with a wire aerial that emerges from the body computer.
Receiver module with 433.92 Mhz working frequency, and the following functions:
- to receive and decode signals from the sending unit;
- store up to 8 transmitters;
- generate a door opening and closure command (by exiting blinker control, if required);
- turn the alarm system on and off.
- generate a timed courtesy light activation command.
The remote control and receiver system has two operating modes:
- on;
- off.
ON CONTROL
At the on control, the receiver sends a signal to the NBC, which:
- implements door locking
- controls a change in alarm system status from rest to surveillance if the BC is designed to do this.
The on command is issued by pressing a key on the sending unit: it is indicated by the turn signals coming on for 2.5 s (lthe signal is enabled/disabled via the EEPROM).
Activation is permanently inhibited (except during diagnosis) with the +15 key-on signal present.
When the key is pressed, the sending unit LED flashing frequency is 3 Hz.
The sending unit transmits the full rolling code in response to continuous pressure on the key lasting at least 50 ms.
If the key is held down continuously, the sending unit interrupts transmission after 20s. To continue transmitting, release the button on the sending unit and press again.
If the receiver detects a continuous transmission (code received always the same), after the first status switch, it excludes the possibility of continuous command switching.
ON
The receiver acquires the rolling code, compares it with codes stored during the programming stage and identifies it from among them.
Once the code has been recognised, the receiver locks the doors and changes the alarm from rest to surveillance mode if the BC is designed to do this.
If the BC contains an alarm system, if the vehicle has been locked beforehand using a mechanical key, the BC must implement the door lock/alarm activation as indicated below when the sending unit button is activated:
- doors locked with key and alarm off (self-activation time not yet elapsed): no door lock operation and alarm activation;
- doors locked with key and alarm on (self-activation time already elapsed): operation of door lock (opening) and alarm deactivation;
- doors released and alarm off (self-activation time not yet elapsed): operation of door lock (locking) and alarm activation;
- doors released and alarm on (self-activation time already elapsed): no door lock operation and alarm deactivation;
DEACTIVATION
Once the receive has received an off command from the sending unit, it sends a message to the NBC which:
- controls door release.
- controls a change in alarm system status from surveillance to rest if the BC is designed to do this.
The system is turned off by pressing the key on the sending unit: the signal is issued by two flashes of the blinkers at 1 Hz, d.c. 50% (function enabled/disabled via the EEPROM).
Deactivation is enabled even with the +15 signal present.
The receiver controls release according to the rules described in the activation paragraph (only if lock status is active).
Alarm system deactivation is also controlled.
For more details on the sending unit.
See descriptions 5520 ENGINE STARTING [→939003530 5520 ENGINE STARTING]

#### PROGRAMMING THE ELECTRONIC KEY (TEG)
The electronic key is programmed at end of line together with the ALFA CODE.
During the vehicle's lifetime, it is possible to make the TEG Reader (NTR) learn new keys, e.g. if ELECTRONIC KEYS (TEGs) are added or deleted.
Upon each new programming procedure, all the Electronic Keys not presented during the above procedure (for the removal of lost keys) are cleared from the memory.
All available TEGs must be programed upon each programming. Those not presented will be deleted from the memory and it will not be possible to program them.

##### Procedure for storing an electronic key teg
The TEG storage procedure is managed by the Diagnostic instrument (Examiner) and can be activated only by entering the ELECTRONIC CODE (shown on the CODE CARD).
The procedure consists of learning the TEG codes and involves secret codes being received by the TEG Reader and then stored. During the procedure, the codes are stored permanently in the TEG Reader EEPROM memory.
Once the procedure is activated, the flow is as follows:
- the Diagnostic instrument commands the TEG Reader to initialise the TEG learning procedure and confirms this to the operator;
- the operator enters the first TEG to be stored;
- the TEG Reader receives the secret code and the ID of the ELECTRONIC KEY (TEG) and learns it;
- the Diagnostic instrument confirms that learning has taken place;
- the previous stages are repeated for each TEG that must be learned, up to a maximum of 8;
- once the TEGs have been learned, the operator asks the Diagnostic instrument to store them: the Diagnostic instrument commands the TEG Reader to store the TEGs learnt.
Only TEGs learned during the procedure are stored in the EEPROM. Any TEGs no longer presented will not be stored.

##### Code system component managment
There is a centralized DATA BASE (for all markets) managed by the FIAT PARTS DIVISION for ordering all CODE system components.
The production plant transfers all the necessary data into this data base together at the time of vehicle production.
FIAT PARTS then uses this data base for ordering components that need replacing by the Dealer Network.
The data base contains numerous pieces of information, such as:
- vehicle chassis no.;
- secret code;
- code of each ELECTRONIC KEY (TEG);
- emergency key mechanical code;
- programming date.
If one of the CODE system components needs replacing and is being ordered, follow the procedure described below.

##### Lost teg
Ask the Customer for all the remaining TEGs in their possession.
The Customer must prove that he or she is the owner of the vehicle by producing the registration document and identification data.
The codes of the lost TEGs must be cleared from the memory of the TEG Reader: proceed as follows:
1. Connect the Tester to the tester output on the vehicle.
2. Set the TEG Reader to PROGRAMMING mode.
3. Enter the TEGs still in the driver's possession into the TEG Reader.
4. End PROGRAMMING mode; the IDs of any TEGs not presented will be cleared from the TEG Reader memory.
At the end of the procedure, print a table showing the identification code/s still enabled. If no printer is available, copy the codes from the screen onto the FIAT PARTS system form.
Only if the Body Computer already contains 8 ELECTRONIC KEYS (TEGs) send the codes to Fiat Parts to update the DATABASE.

##### Request for a new teg
Use the Personal Computer supplied to log onto Fiat Parts. Enter the chassis no. of the customer's car, the model code and set up a VOR order to request a new TEG (entering the part number) and specify the quantity.
Note that the Body Computer is designed to store up to 8 TEGs. It is not therefore possible to accept orders when the sum of the number of TEGs already available to the customer plus the new TEGs ordered exceed this quantity. Keep a record of the form used to order the TEGs in order to monitor the situation.

##### Programming teg codes into the teg reader memory
Once the new TEGs have been received from Fiat Parts, ensure that all the old TEGs in the customer's possession are available.
Connect the Tester to the vehicle tester output and run the following procedure.
1. Set the TEG Reader to PROGRAMMING mode.
2. Enter the TEGs still in the driver's possession into the TEG Reader.
3. End PROGRAMMING mode; the IDs of any TEGs not presented will be cleared from the TEG Reader memory.
4. Check system operation before returning the vehicle to the customer by starting it up using all the TEGs and opening/closing the doors using the remote control unit.
> Note: In the case of operating faults, it is possible to order spare parts only, but it is absolutely forbidden to exchange electronic control units between different TEGs because it will not be possible to service the vehicle in the future.

##### Replacing lock barrels and/or emergency mechanical keys
This becomes necessary when one or more door lock barrels (driver's door lock or others) are forced.
The Customer must prove that he or she is the owner of the vehicle by producing the registration document and identification data.
Use the Personal Computer supplied to log onto Fiat Parts. Enter the chassis no. of the customer's car, the model code and set up a VOR order to order a single electronic key kit complete with dowels (entering the part number) for the vehicle type and specification.
> Note: It is not possible to order a single barrel by giving a single mechanical code.
> Note: The mechanical code of the emergency key and the electronic code of the TEG are defined together during initial memorisation on a vehicle at end of line and must not be separated under any circumstances.

##### Replacing the reg reader
Ask the Customer for all the remaining TEGs in their possession.
They should also prove that they are the owner of the vehicle by producing the registration document and identification data.
Use the Personal Computer supplied to log onto Fiat Parts. Enter the chassis no. of the customer's car, the model code and set up a VOR order to order a single TEG Reader (entering the part number to identify the version).
Once the new programmed TEG Reader has been received from Fiat Parts, proceed as follows:
1. Check the serial number stamped on the plate applied to the order form corresponds to that shown on the TEG Reader.
2. Check the vehicle chassis no. printed on the plate applied to the order form corresponds to the vehice chassis no.
3. If all codes correspond, install the TEG Reader on the vehicle instead of the malfunctioning unit.
4. Connect the Tester to the tester output on the vehicle.
5. Set the TEG Reader to PROGRAMMING mode.
6. Enter the TEGs still in the driver's possession into the TEG Reader.
7. End PROGRAMMING mode; the IDs of any TEGs not presented will be cleared from the TEG Reader memory (NTR).
8. Check system operation before returning the vehicle to the customer by starting it up using all the TEGs and opening/closing the doors using the remote control unit.

##### Replacing the engine management control unit
This is required if the engine malfunctions.
The Customer must prove that he or she is the owner of the vehicle by producing the registration document and identification data.
Use the personal computer provided to log onto Fiat Parts. Enter the part number of the Engine Control Unit to be replaced.
Once the Engine Control Unit has been received from Fiat Parts, install it on the vehicle and insert the TEG in the TEG Reader to allow self-programming.
Press the START/STOP button with the clutch or brake depressed to start the vehicle and check the engine is operating correctly.

##### Replacing the electric steering lock (nbs)
This is required if the electric steering lock malfunctions.
The Customer must prove that he or she is the owner of the vehicle by producing the registration document and identification data.
Use the personal computer provided to log onto Fiat Parts. Enter the part number of the Electric Steering Lock to be replaced.
Once the Electric Steering Lock has been received from Fiat Parts, install it on the vehicle and insert the TEG in the TEG Reader to allow self-programming.
After 10s, remove the TEG from the TEG Reader and wait for the steering to lock mechanically (this will take place after approx 5s). Check that the steering is locked.

##### Replace the body computer (nbc)
This is required if the Body Computer malfunctions.
The Customer must prove that he or she is the owner of the vehicle by producing the registration document and identification data.
Use the Personal Computer supplied to log onto Fiat Parts. Enter the chassis no. of the customer's car, the model code and set up a VOR order to order a single Body Computer (entering the part number to identify the version).
Once the Body Computer has been received from Fiat Parts, install it on the vehicle and insert the TEG in the TEG Reader to allow alignment of the Secret Codes.
Press the START/STOP button with the clutch or brake depressed to start the vehicle and check the vehicle electrics are operating correctly.

## 5580H PARKING OBSTACLE DETECTION DEVICE  [939003539]
- Path: Descriptions > 55 ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT > 5580 SPECIAL ACCESSORIES > 5580H PARKING OBSTACLE DETECTION DEVICE
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939003539

#### INTRODUCTION
The "Parking Assistance" system supplies the driver with information on distance when approaching obstacles (both behind and in front of the vehicle) thereby providing help with parking manoeuvres and identifying obstacles that are outside the field of vision.
The information concerning the presence or distance of the obstacle is transmitted to the driver by means of acoustic and visual signals.
- the frequency of the acoustic impulse warnings depends on the distance of the obstacle from the bumper.
- the display in the instrument panel shows the areas around the vehicle which start flashing if the system detects that the vehicle is getting close to an obstacle.
The distance measurement only takes place when the system is activated, whilst only the control unit is operational in the inactive state.
The parking assistance system comprises the following components:
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939000071.jpg]
1 - electronic control unit
2 - ultrasound sensors located in the front bumper
3 - front speaker (buzzer)
4 - ultrasound sensors located in the rear bumper
5 - rear speaker (buzzer)
6 - instrument panel display
7 - system activation/deactivation button

#### OPERATION

##### Activation and deactivation of the system
The system is activated if the following conditions are present simultaneously:
- Key ON
- Reverse gear engaged or activation button pressed (with the speed below 15 km/h).
When the system is activated the buzzer warns of this condition and the LED is lit up.
The system is deactivated:
- by pressing the button again
- by disengaging reverse gear and when the vehicle speed is above 18 km/h.
The LED goes out when the system is deactivated.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939000072.jpg]
1 - system activation/deactivation button
2 - system activated LED

##### Obstacle distance acoustic signals
The control unit processes information supplied by sensors, operating the two buzzers to signal the presence of any obstacles.
The sound from the buzzer warns the driver that the vehicle is approaching an obstacle. The sound lasts for 75 ms, whilst the pause between the sounds is directly proportional to the distance of the obstacle: impulses in quick succession indicate the presence of an obstacle that is very close. A continuous sound indicates that the obstacle is less than 30 cm away.
The acoustic signal stops immediately if the distance of the obstacle increases. The sound cycle remains constant if the distance measured by the centre sensors remains unchanged, whilst if this situation occurs for the side sensors, the signal is interrupted after 3 seconds (for example, to prevent signals in the case of manoeuvres alongside walls).

##### Obstacle distance visual signals
The control unit processes information supplied by sensors, sending the information to the instrument panel for signalling the presence of any obstacles.
The instrument panel display with the system activated shows the various areas around the vehicle, 7 front and 8 rear.
The various areas in the different cases are either off, flashing or on constantly in accordance with the following logic (SEE DIAGRAM):
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939000073.jpg]
example:
- obstacle in the right rear area (sectors H and I)
- obstacle still far away: sectors H and I both off
- the obstacle is getting closer: sector I is flashing, sector H remains switched off
- the obstacle is getting even closer: sector H is on constantly, sector I goes out; the situation is similar for the other sectors.
In the case of large obstacles (e.g. walls) one and only one sector is lit up at a time.

##### Autodiagnosis and recovery
The control unit carries out an autodiagnostic test when it is switched on. The sensors are diagnosed every time they are activated. A fault even in only one sensor inhibits the operation of the entire system which is deactivated.
The errors detected by the control unit can be read via the CAN using suitable diagnostic equipment (Examiner).

##### Error signalling
Any faults/errors are signalled in the instrument panel by the relevant warning light coming on and the message "PARKING ASSISTANCE NOT AVAILABLE" in the display.
> Note: The warning signals that the system is not available without any reference to the faulty sensor or the type of fault.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939000074.jpg]

#### COMPONENT SPECIFICATIONS

##### Parking sensor control unit (cpa)
The control unit is an electronic component connected to the rear wiring that manages the assistance function by carrying out the following functions:
- receiving the button activation/deactivation signals via the CAN and directly
- activating the operating LED
- activating the sensors
- processing the signals received by the sensors
- checking the operation of the sensors
- operating the buzzers
- managing the fault diagnosis and test functions
The electronic control unit has a device that protects against voltage fluctuations and short circuits.
It is located in the luggage compartment, on the right rear side panel; it is connected with three connectors:
- CONNECTOR A (rear wiring) control unit power supply and signals from other nodes or vehicle components;
- CONNECTOR B (front wiring) front bumper sensors power supply;
- CONNECTOR C (rear wiring) rear bumper sensors power supply.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939000075.jpg]

###### Control unit pin out

| --- | --- |

| 3 | n.c. |

##### Ultrasound sensors
The sensor is an ultrasound transducer which acts as an intelligent transmitter and receiver of ultrasound impulse packages. Both the frequency and the voltage of the impulses are produced in the transducer.
The impulses emitted are reflected by any obstacles; the transducer therefore receives an echo which is amplified and converted into a digital signal, sent to the electronic control unit via the same line used for the transmission request.
Each sensor can also be operated as a receiver only, in order to be able to take a triangular measurement between two sensors.
This technique allows better detection of small obstacles and in situations featuring critical reflection.
The sensors all have the same electrical and mechanical properties; the maximum detection distance for each sensor can be adjusted using software according to the location of the actual sensor.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939000076.jpg]

###### Sensor pin out
| Pin | Signal |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Sensor power supply |
| 2 | Sensor signal |
| 3 | Sensor earth |

##### Acoustic signals
Two buzzers, one at the front and one at the rear, notify the driver of the following information:
- activation of the system;
- distance of the obstacle;
- a possible fault in the system.
The frequency and the volume of the signalling can be controlled by the control unit.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939000077.jpg]

###### Location
The front buzzer is located on the cover under the dashboard on the driver's side.
The rear buzzer is located in the luggage compartment at the base of the right rear pillar.

## 5580P CONNECT PANEL  [939003540]
- Path: Descriptions > 55 ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT > 5580 SPECIAL ACCESSORIES > 5580P CONNECT PANEL
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939003540

#### CONNECT NAV + DESCRIPTION
Dimensions: 2DIN box with front panel
Modules included:
- Radio
- CD player - Audio + CD - MP3 ROM
- GPS navigation system module
- GSM phone module
- Independent navigation with maps
- Independent navigation with maps
- Assistance services
- 256 colour 6.5" TFT display
- External CD CHANGER system (if present)
- Built-in voice recognition module
- WAP protocol

##### Internal modules
The system modules or the modules to which the system can be connected for obtaining information or requesting services are different.

###### Cd rom player
CONNECT is equipped with a CD ROM player that is able to read and manage CD ROMs and audio CDs. The Audio media may be normal commercial audio CDs or CD ROMs containing files in MP3 format (all levels). Other acceptable ROM media include official Marelli media that contain an updated copy of the CONNECT management software and also the map database required for navigation.

###### Cd changer
CONNECT is also designed to be connected to an external CD Changer and to accept analogue audio output.

###### Gsm module
The CONNECT system is equipped with a GSM Dual Band module and micro format SIM Card reader (that allows the user the insert a SIM Card). There is also an external microphone (for hands free use and voice recognition) and preparation for the connection of a hand set.

###### Radio - cd module
General specifications:
- Music audio power: 4x35W
- 5 band graphic equalizer

##### System activation
The CONNECT system may be activated in two different modes:
- Automatic activation with the ignition key ON
- Manual activation by means of ON button
- Emergency manual activation by means of SOS button

###### Automatic activation
When the ignition key is turned to MAR position, the CONNECT system turns on automatically to make all the functions described in this chapter active or enabled.

###### Manual activation
With the ignition key in STOP position, the CONNECT system comes on when the ON button is pressed to make the following modes available:
- MAIN
- AUDIO
- NAV
- TEL
- SOS and SERVICE (Targasys)
> Note: In this mode, the SETUP and TRIP modules can be activated but it is not possible to validate any parameter change, language change or measurement unit change or any other type of adjustment envisaged by the CONNECT system. These limitations are normal when the system is activated by means of the ON button. When the vehicle is not running (key OFF), the data transmission devices inside the vehicle are not operational. When ignition key is turned ON, the system begins to work.

##### System deactivation
The CONNECT system may be activated in two different modes:
- deactivation independent of the ignition key
- deactivation dependent on the ignition key

###### Deactivation independent of the ignition key
When this mode is active, the CONNECT system may be turned off by pressing the ON button.
The display shows the message DEACTIVATION PROCEDURE IN PROGRESS, WAIT A FEW MOMENTS.
> Note: With the ignition key OFF, the system deactivates with a delay of 20 minutes if a system destination has been set or if a phone conversation is in progress.

###### Deactivation dependent on the ignition key
When this mode is active, the CONNECT system may be turned off by turning the ignition key to STOP.

##### Languages available
The following languages are available for both strings of displayed text (menus) and navigation voice messages: Italian, English, French, German, Spanish and Portuguese.
The voice recognition unit language may be set independently of the menu and navigation message language. The same languages are available.

##### Code activation and recognition procedure
The Connect (NIT) includes an ANTITHEFT function that prevents it operating in the case of theft.
The NIT is installed during producition and connnected to the CAN network in order to establish communication with the Body Computer and store an antitheft code known as the Exchange Code.
At each subsequent Key On (and even if the battery is disconnected), an automatic authentication procedure is repeated: if the Exchange Code check is positive, the system begins to operate. If the codes compared are not the same, a message appears on the display asking the user to enter a manual code (Master Code - 4-figure code from 1111 to 6666) that is shown on the radio code card.
> Note: The Master Code is pre-programmed in production and different for each NIT. It is also different from the Exchange Code.
[image: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/media/939000082.jpg]
> Note: The manual Master Code input procedure is necessary only if:- the Body Computer is replaced- an NIT is installed that has already been used on another vehicle with a CAN network
> Note: a new NIT (never installed on other vehicles) may be fitted using an automatic authentication procedure without manual input of the Master Code.

#### AUDIO MODULE

##### Audio sources
Possible audio sources include standard sources (Radio Tuner, Audio CD/MP3 and CD Changer) whose specifications are detailed in the rest of the chapter. PTY31 Alarms (Program TYpe) and Traffic Announcements, Sources linked to other modules such as the telephone, telephone ringing, voice recognition and voice synthesis for navigation are treated as separate functions.

###### Standard source
One of the standard sources is activated (possibly interrupted by a Traffic Announcement). The navigation messages are available.

###### Phone call in progress
A telephone call is activated. If it is an incoming call, the source activated before the phonecall will be restored at the end of the conversation. The navigation messages are available.

###### Ringing
Sound to indicate incoming call. The navigation messages are not available.

###### Voice recognition
The dialogue between the recognizer and the user is activated. The navigation messages are not available.

###### Pty31 alarm
Due to the receipt of a PTY31 message from the tuner. The navigation messages are available.

###### Tuner function
FM, MW and LW tuner with RDS, EON, PTY and TP management. If a voice recognition module is fitted, several of the commands can be voice-activated.

###### Cd audio function
The Audio CD/MP3 source and hence the function can be selected from amongst the various audio sources on the CONNECT unit.
Various commands are available to the user through the direct buttons (front panel/steering wheel controls) and those selected from the menu on the screen If a voice recognition module is fitted, several of the commands can be voice-activated.

###### External cd changer management
The CD Changer source (Audio) and hence the function can be selected from amongst the various audio sources on the Connect unit. This function is only available if the CONNECT is connected to an external CD Changer of the type described previously.
Various commands are available to the user through the direct buttons (front panel/steering wheel controls) and those selected from the menu on the screen If a voice recognition module is fitted, several of the commands can be voice-activated.

###### Cd - mp3 mode
The Connect systemis able to recognise the type of compact disc inserted.
During the recognition stage, the display shows the message "Reading CD... " and then the system detects whether the CD inserted contains musical tracks recorded in MP3 mode (e.g. music files with the extension .mp3).
> Note: The MP3 track names must not include the characters Open and Close Brackets “(“ “)“, otherwise the Connect system will be unable to play the tracks.
The Connect system automatically organises the tracks present on the CD in mp3 format into folders and creates sequential ists of all folders that contain MP3 tracks.
A CD could contain thousands of mp3 files. In this case, a maximum limit is set for the number of files managed. The system will consider only the first 999 music tracks and the display shows the following message for about 7 seconds: "Attention, only the first 999 MP3 CD tracks will be managed by the system
Once the MP3 CD is inserted and recognised by the system, the main screen shows the following functions:

##### Functions available to the user
The phone module allows normal phone activity, text messages, support for Service Calls to the Provider (described in the relevant chapter) and Internet access by means of WAP (Wireless Access Protocol).

###### Phone functions
The phone module is used to:
- accept an incoming phone call.
- refuse an incoming call
- send a phone call

###### Sim data base access functions
The SIM Card database allows the following options:
- Read the list of phone numbers saved on the SIM card.
- Enter a phone number on the SIM
- Delete a phone number from the SIM.
- Copy the contents of a SIM phoneboook to the CONNECT phonebook and viceversa.
- Copy the contents of a SIM phonebook on another SIM.
Information is also provided on the status of the SIM (SIM Card corrected or incorrectly inserted) and the space available in the SIM memory.

###### Last number functions
The module is able to store the last 10 numbers called to help the user with repeat calls.

###### Sms message functions
The module manages text messages for the user and also from the Service Provider. It is therefore possibile:
- to display received messages that have not yet been read (full list or selected message).
- to display received messages that have been read or saved (full list or selected message).
- save a received message.
- delete a message (recently received or already saved).
- send a message to a particular number entered by the user.
- set up the Service Provider number for text messages.

###### Gsm status display functions
It is possible to obtain information on:
- aerial signal quality
- network operator's name
- presence of text messages received but not yet read.

###### Configuration functions
"Call divert": incoming calls can be diverted to another phone number, specifying the type (Voice, Data..)
Network operater management: the module manages network operator selection (manual or automatic search) and also the user of a list of preferred operators (display, delete, input and overwrite functions).
Security: use of PIN code, PUK, display number of PIN input attempts remaining before PUK code requested, change PIN code.
Access to a WAP site requires data to be loaded into the memory (in technical terms: loading of the deck) and the first page (card) is not displayed until the end of the operation. The central part of the screen shows the text, links and selection/input options. The right side of the display shows the software keys (Vertical softkey) that are used to activate the possible card actions (max 6, usually in English).
For example, the following functions may be shown:
For example, the following functions may be shown:

The lower bar shows browser functions that can be activated by means of the reconfigurable keys, described below:
- “Home”: access to the page set up as Home.

##### Procedure for general use
Before the phone module can be used, the user must enter a PIN security code whenever the CONNECT system is turned on after being turned off (unless "exclude PIN request" has been set under Settings). Unless the PIN code is entered, the system can be used only for emergency calls (112 in Italy) and not normal user calls or for the Service Call function.
If an incorrect PIN is entered three times, the module is bound to request the PUK code to release the block.

###### Engine management by steering wheel
The phone module can be partly controlled by the buttons on the steering wheel.

###### Audio status repetition on the control panel display
The CONNECT module sends various information to the control panel via the CAN network on phone section operating status.

##### Voice recognition
Voice recognition module with speaker dependent functions (Phonebook, Navigation address book, Radio Station memory) and speaker independent functions for Radio, CD, CDC, Phone and Services, Navigation System. The speaker dependent function allows a voice command (prerecorded by the user) to be associated with a phone number in the phonebook, a stored radio station or a destination present in the destination list (personal).
The speaker independent functions allow the activation of general controls (e.g.: "Radio Autostore", "CD play", "Navigatore Zoom", ...).

###### Voice command
After pressing the VR key, the user can speak a voice command. The module compares the sample with those present in its memory and, if recognised, allows the relevant command to be activated (call one fo the phone numbers in the phonebook, select one of the preset stations as an audio source, start the autostore procedure for the radio stations in the current band, change to CD source, etc...) The system guides the user using voice information (Example - After pressing the VR key, the user says: "Call number" and the Connect responds: "Number please").

###### Speaker dependent functions
RECORDING RADIO VOICE COMMAND: When storing a radio station in one of the positions available in the radio bands (FM1, FM2, FM3….), the user can associate it with a voice command. Upon the user's request, this gives rise to an initialisation stage when the module asks for a voice command to be entered and repeated and then confirms recording.
RECORDING PHONE (NAVIGATION SYSTEM) VOICE COMMAND: When entering a number and associated name in the phone book the user can associate a voice command with this item in the same way as with the radio stations.
RECORDING NAVIGATION SYSTEM VOICE COMMAND: When entering a destination in the navigation system address book the user can associate a voice command with this item in the same way as with the radio stations.
DELETING A VOICE COMMAND: The voice commands described above may be deleted or modified.

###### Speaker independent functions
The system does not require an initialisation stage to use this function (i.e. recording of voice samples by the user). Although the terminology has been designed to include commonly used phrases, it is nevertheless advisable to read the keyword table in the Connect User Handbook. As an example, the keywords for the CD player are given below.
LANGUAGES AVAILABLE: The following languages are availalbe for requests and communication with the user: Italian, English, French, German, Spanish and European Portuguese.

###### Record voice messages
This module, known as the Voice Memo, allows the user to record and re-enter voice messages up to 3 minutes long. The messages are recorded sequentially in the frame and a warning message is displayed if the memory contains messages.
Recording: the recording activated by the user can last up to 3 minutes and terminates automatically when the available time is up. The user can interrupt the recording manually in any case.

###### Voice memo
The following functions are available:
- Play: plays the message
- Stop : interrupts playback or recording
- SKIP : skips to the next message
- SKIP : skips to the previous message
- Record: Starts recording
- Delete: clears the message memory (individual frames cannot be deleted).

###### Wap mode
The term WAP stands for: WIRELESS APPLICATION PROTOCOL.
WAP technology makes it possible to access the Internet using a mobile phone when no computer is available.
WAP browsing is relatively similar to conventional browsing on the PC but the same performance cannot be expected as with PC Internet access and an ADSL (“Asymmetric Digital Subscriber Line”: a technique that allows data to be transferred at high speed over normal phone lines using special Modems) because the graphics are very poor with WAP and the information is reduced to the essentials.
Because WAP technology is specific, mobile phones cannot be used to access ordinary WEB sites as with a PC.
The Internet supports WEB pages produced with language such as HTML (“Hyper Text Markup Language”: the international language of electronic texts - hypertexts) that are displayed on a PC by means of BROWSERS (Navigators, such as: NETSCAPE NAVIGATOR, INTERNET EXPLORER, etc…).
WAP is based on a different language: WML (Wireless Markup Language) with its own Script (another word for Program. usually indicates a program written in a particular language to perform tasks connected with the operating system) with its own image formats and also requiring its own , BROWSER or MICRO- BROWSER to display WEB pages.
These BROWSERS are built into the latest WAP mobile phones: if you enter the required settings (indicated below), you are able to access the required WAP sites.
For WAP phones, addresses are also in “ HTTP:// ”; the format used for the WEB.
WAP pages are located on an HTTP Server and their technical operation is as follows: when a WAP address is entered on the display of a mobile phone, the phone forwards an HTTP request for a WML page resident on a WEB Server.
The request is received over the GSM network by the WAP GATEWAY that forwards it to the WEB Server by means of a coding/decoding procedure.
At this point, the requested page returns to the WAP GATEWAY that codes/decodes it to route it to the mobile phone that originated the request.
This is what happens when the requested content is already in WML format (for mobile phones).
The requested pages are often in HTML format (for PC). In this case, the WAP GATEWAY acts as a HTML - WML translator in real time.
> Note: In the case of complex sites with lots of graphics, the result on the mobile display could be illegible.

###### Text messages
In TEL mode, the user can access the OTHER MENUS screen from the main menu and then select the text message service (Short Message Service - SMS) that allows the reading and sending of short messages up to 160 characters via the GSM phone.
> Note: Refer to the Owner's Handbook for user instructions.
Remember that to user the text message service, you need to enter the Phone Number of the Service Centre of the Service Provider that the user intends to use.
To set the service centre phone number, select the following from the text message (SMS) menu: "Centre number".
Dial the Service Centre telephone number using the multifunction keys (the service centre phone number is supplied by the user's SIM card network provider).
When in OTHER MENUS, select OPTIONS to display the following menu:
- Network operator: to select a Network Provider.
- PIN: to manage the PIN code.
- Information: to display information on the GSM module (Provider name, IMEI code (International Mobile Equipement Identity), etc…).

#### NAVIGATION SYSTEM MODULE

##### Operation
The navigation system allows you to reach a destination set by the user by giving visual and acoustic instructions.
The navigation module built into the NIT receives data on progress (forward motion and reverse) and direction changes from information made available on the CAN network by the NBC. It cross-checks this with information received from GPS satellites by means of the GPS aerial on the car roof to calculate the Estimated Car Point (car location).
> Note: The navigation module does not contain a gyroscope because if no signals are received from the satelllites, the Navigation system recognises the car's motion using vehicle motion information received from the CAN network.
Upon initial activation and each time the battery is disconnected, the GPS takes about 15 minutes to activate.
The navigation system takes about 100km to self-regulate accurately from the first system start-up and when the tyres are changed.
If the engine is turned off and the vehicle is moved with the system off (e.g. on a pick-up truck), at the next key-on, the GPS system will take a few minutes to determine the car's new position.
The navigation CD-ROM drive is located on the front of the Connect system and is the same as used for audio CDs.
It is not therefore possible to use the audio player and the navigation drive simultaneously: The navigation system can, however, work partly even without the navigation CD-ROM inserted.

###### Route guidance
The main function of the Navigation module is called Route Guidance. This is responsible for extracting, managing and processing the information required to guide the user to the set destination.
These activities are, basically:
- ROUTE CALCULATION: Calculation of the route between the current position and the destination. Route calculation with multiple destinations. Route recalculation in the case of deviation from the current route. Calculation of an alternative route.
- TRUE ROUTE GUIDANCE: Identification of the position of the vehicle on the route (and calculation of the distance to the destination); Identification of junctions along the route; Identification of manoeuvres at the junctions along the route (and graphic and voice instructions for the user): Calculation of the distance to the next junction where the user has to make a turn; junction zoom function in built-up areas.
- DIGITAL MAPS: The official M. MARELLI CD ROM contains a Map Database that is made available to all other system functions. Access to any map data (segments, areas, locations etc.) required by other modules takes place through one of the functions available on this CD ROM.
- COMPLETE DATA BASE MANAGEMENT: If a map CD-ROM is present, the navigation function uses the entire data base available (map list, points of interest, etc.).
- USE OF REDUCED DATABASE WHEN CD-ROM NOT PRESENT (LISTENING TO A MUSIC CD): It is possible to listen to an audio CD in the CD player during the navigation process. Simply following the procedure described. The map CD should be inserted in the CD player for the entire duration of the entering the destination and route calculation activities. At the end of this processing, the CD ROM can be removed using the eject button. At this point the system will: 1) automatically load the route calculated into the memory; 2) eject the map CD. The audio CD can now be inserted to start listening. Under these circumstances one part of the map information is available (names of towns and names of roads) relating only to the segments of the route. In any case, the reduced data base in the CONNECT memory allows deviations to the route with automatic recalculations without the need to reinsert the CD-ROM. However, the efficiency of these recalculations depends very much on the length of the original route. When the route data in the memory is not sufficient to continue the navigation process, there is a request to reinsert the map CD. If the system is switched off during navigation without a CD ROM, the next time it is switched back on, the map CD must be inserted to access the navigation functions.
With the key ON, the Connect and Navigation system mobile are activated. A message appears reminding the customer that the navigation system is a tool that can help guide through traffic but the reponsibility always lies with the driver and the highway code must be respected at all times. ##### Address book
The CONNECT contains two different address books: one for the phone and the other for the navigation system. The purpose of both is to make it easier to enter data (a phone number or destination) required by the user without going through a long procedure each time.
This operation may be carried out once only and the result is saved in CONNECT and associated with a memorable name. Then all you have to do is identify a saved option by selecting from a list or entering the memorable name.
Both address books are also stored in a back up memory (flash memory). This means that information stored persists even after the system has been turned on and off or after the battery has been disconnected.

###### Phonebook
The following fields are present in the phone book:
- name: memorable label for fast access to the list.
- Phone number: number used by CONNECT for calls.
- Position: origin of the item in the list.
- Voice recognition: voice sample for activation via voice recognition.
Name and number may be entered by the user during creation of a new address book item. In this case, the origin field indicates that the item is stored permanently in the CONNECT internal address book. Or Name and Number may be present on the SIM Card that the user has entered in the CONNECT SIM Reader. The System also displays this information as phone book items. After the Card has been inserted, the address book management module reads all the items on the Card and makes a copy by creating new temporary items if the name/number pair is not already present in the CONNECT address book. In this case, the position field indicates that the item comes from the SIM CARD.
This item type is deleted from the address book when it is downloaded or the system is turned off.
The following phone book functions are available to the user:
- enter new item
- delete all items in the phonebook
- listen to/delete all voice samples recorded by the user
- select item (open detailed window).
Detailed window:
- sent call to the selected number
- modify an individual item (name, number, listen/modify)
delete an individual voice sample:
- delete an individual item
- save an individual item in the Frequent Number list.
It is also possible to copy all the items from the CONNECT phonebook to the SIM Card and viceversa.
It is also possible to copy the contents of the phonebook on the SIM Card inserted to another SIM Card.
> Note: In any case, the content of the target phonebook will be completely overwritten.

###### Navigation system address book
The following fields are present in the navigation address book:
- name: memorable label for fast access to the list.
- Description of geographical location defined by user: string consisting of town name/street name or name of associated POI...
- Voice sample
- Co-ordinates: place co-ordinates (not visible to user and used internally for localisation or route calculation).
- The item may be entered in the address book when the destination is entered. It is also possible to associate a voice sample to be used to call up the address by means of the voice recognition function.
The functions available to the user for the address book are similar to those available for the phone book:
- delete existing item
- select item
- modify.
> Note: Refer to the Owner's Handbook for more detailed user instructions.

The Trip Computer module integral with the Connect manages and calculates a lot of information that can then be displayed on screen to supply a set of useful data on the route followed by the user.
Some information comes directly from the Navigation module, others comes from the various vehicle Nodes. For this reason, the Trip computer is fully operational only when the the ignition is ON and the network wakes up and can carry information required by the Trip Computer.

#### EMERGENCY (SOS) AND ASSISTANCE (Targasys) SERVICES
The emergency, information and assistance services are managed by TARGASYS
The Connect makes two keys available for activating different Services.
- SOS KEY allows the activation of functions strictly connected with Rescue Services (doctor, roadside rescue) managed on subscription by TARGASYS (a paid service available as an option), a personal number and the EMERGENCY number 112 (always available, even without a SIM card inserted).
- CONNECT KEY: allows the activation of operations linked to information Services managed under subscription by TARGASYS.
> Note: The provision of services is based on a phone connection between the vehicle and the Service exchange. If the SIM Card enabled for Service provision is not inserted, the services will not be active. If no PIN code is entered when services are requested, the user will be notified of the need to enter the PIN code but it will not be requested. Assistance calls can be activated if the mobile phone offers this function and is properly powered. In the case of accidents of vehicle damage, such calls may not be available.
> Note: Refer to the Owner's Handbook for user instructions.

- MEDICAL ADVICE: this function is present only if TARGASYS services are enabled.
- ROADSIDE ASSISTANCE: this function is present only if TARGASYS services are enabled.
- PERSONAL NUMBER: this function is present only if the phone is on and if the SIM card is entered with the PIN keyed in and if the number has been set previously.
- EMERGENCY 112: this function allows a phone call to be made to the number 112 without the need to call up the phone menu and key in the number. 112 is the emergency number for all Countries where this public service is available. An Emergency 112 call can always be made, even if no SIM card is present in the slot.
- SETTINGS: this function allows certain operating modes to be entered and adjusted.
> Note: Refer to the Owner's Handbook for more detailed user instructions.

#### SELF-DIAGNOSIS
A Self-Diagnostic function known as ASSISTANCE can be run on the Connect.
Proceed as follows to activate this function:

- Then press the keys relating to the CONNECT icon at the bottom right of the screen

Select ASSISTANCE and then from the next screen SPEAKER TEST: a sound test will be carried out on all speakers to check their operation.
Move to: NEXT MENU and press the knob to display a screen that shows the outcome of tests performed on the Connect.
The Connect constantly carries out internal diagnostics, diagnosis of the FM/AM and GPS aerials and a diagnosis of the speakers. The GSM aerial is not tested.

## 7005 PASSENGER COMPARTMENT FRONT SIDE DOORS  [939003544]
- Path: Descriptions > 70 FITTINGS > 7005 PASSENGER COMPARTMENT FRONT SIDE DOORS
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939003544

#### CONTROLS
The controls for the following functions are located on the driver's door panel trim:
- driver's front window opening/closing;
- passenger side front window opening/closing;
- left rear window opening/closing;
- right rear window opening/closing;
- rear electric windows lock;
- exterior rear view mirror joystick.
The buttons for opening/closing the passenger front window are located on the passenger door panel trim.

#### OPERATION
> Note: All the functions described here are managed by the two door control units and the luggage compartment control unit (for the rear doors)See descriptions 5505 INSTRUMENT/GAUGE ELECTRICAL CIRCUITS [→939003529 5505 INSTRUMENT/GAUGE ELECTRICAL CIRCUITS]

##### Door locking / unlocking
The simultaneous operation of the four door locks takes place via:
- - TEG the remote control;
- - the locking/unlocking button in the centre console.
The TEG remote has 3 buttons which allow the operation of the central locking system: a button for unlocking the doors, one for locking the vehicle and one for releasing the boot.
See descriptions 5520 ENGINE STARTING [→939003530 5520 ENGINE STARTING]
> Note: The fuel flap is also locked/unlocked at the same time as the doors, controlled by the same driver's door logic.
> Note: If the remote control fails, insert the metal insert (inside the key) in the lock in the driver's door and turn it.With the central locking on, pulling the interior opening lever for one of the doors causes the closure for all the doors to be released. If there is no electrical power supply the doors can be locked manually
The locks have an additional motor that carries out the dead lock function which allows the interior door opening handles to be mechanically disconnected so that it is no longer possible to open the door from the inside (for example, after having broken the glass in a theft attempt); the dead lock function also inhibits the operation of the door locking/unlocking buttons in the dashboard.
The dead lock function is switched on at the time the doors are locked or by pressing the remote control twice.
The LED in the driver's door produces the following signals:
- Locking the locks: the LED lights up for 3 seconds. If some of the doors or the boot are not properly shut at the time when the locks are locked, the LED flashes at 3 Hz for 3 seconds;
- Dead lock activation: the LED flashes twice for 0.5 seconds;
- Unlocking the locks: the LED goes out.
The doors are automatically unlocked if the inertia switch is operated: the instrument panel receives a signal from the switch, lights up the appropriate warning light and notifies the Body Computer via the CAN.

###### Possible adjustments
It is possible, using the special setup in the instrument panel, to select whether to unlock all the doors or only the driver's front door, whilst all the other doors and the boot remain locked.
It is possible to enable/disable the locking of the doors above a certain speed threshold (20 km/h) using the special setup in the instrument panel: in this case the Body Computer implements the locking of the doors when this threshold is exceeded.
When the speed returns below this level, the doors and the boot remain locked; later on, when one of the doors is opened, the function is re-enabled and, if the threshold is exceeded, the doors are locked once again.
The boot unlocking operating mode can be selected still using the special setup in the instrument panel:
- assisted boot unlocking: the tailgate is considered as a fifth door to all intents and purposes;
- indepedent boot unlocking: the boot is locked when the doors are locked, whilst it can be unlocked independently of the unlocking of the doors.

##### Front electric windows
The electric windows for the front doors are operated through the switches on the driver's door (both windows) and the passenger side (passenger side only).
Automatic operation takes place as follows:
- if the button is pressed is between 60 and 300 milliseconds, operation is manual. the glass goes up/down only with the key pressed;
- f the key is pressed for longer than 300 milliseconds, operation is automatic: even if the button is released, the glass continues to move up/down until the end of travel position is reached or until the intervention of the anti-crush safety system (if fitted);
- pressing the button again whilst the window is moving stops it in the position it is in;
- if the button is pressed for less than 60 milliseconds, this is ignored (it is treated as an accidental knock).
The windows are automatically opened or closed through the special prolonged (more than 2 seconds) command sent by the TEG remote control button.
Each control unit in the door also manages the anti-crush safety function: it acquires information concerning the possible presence of an obstacle whilst the glass is closing: under these circumstances the control unit immediately interrupts the travel of the window and reverses it to the lower end of travel position.
> Note: If a failure is detected in the system or if the anti-crush safety function is activated 3 times in the space of 1 minute or if there is a failure, the system automatically enters into recovery mode (self-protection).This condition is evident from the window closing by being raised in stages.
If this happens the system restoral procedure must be carried out as follows:
- open the windows;
- extract the key (TEG) from the starting device and then insert it again

##### Rear view mirror adjustment
The door mirrors can be electrically adjusted in two directions using a joystick control located in the door controls on the driver's side: a selection cursor makes it possible to choose either the left or the right mirror.
The button controls two electrical motors located in each of the two mirrors: one motor allows the rotation of the mirror on the horizontal axis, another on the vertical axis.
Another button controls the folding back of the mirrors if required (for example when trying to get through a narrow space).
> Note: On the HIGH version, in addition to moving the door mirrors manually, it is possible to memorize and later on recall 3 positions defined in relation to the position of the driver's seat; the passenger side rear view mirror is also positioned automatically when reverse gear is engaged.

## 7010 PASSENGER COMPARTMENT REAR SIDE DOORS  [939003545]
- Path: Descriptions > 70 FITTINGS > 7010 PASSENGER COMPARTMENT REAR SIDE DOORS
- Kind: system description
- Applies to: all engines; all production periods
- Web: https://sloeber94.github.io/elrnDB/#/939003545

#### CONTROLS
The buttons for opening/closing the window are located on the rear door panel trim.

#### OPERATION
> Note: All the functions described here are managed by the two door control units and the luggage compartment control unit (for the rear doors)See descriptions 5505 INSTRUMENT/GAUGE ELECTRICAL CIRCUITS [→939003529 5505 INSTRUMENT/GAUGE ELECTRICAL CIRCUITS]

##### Door locking / unlocking
The simultaneous operation of the four door locks takes place via:
- - TEG the remote control;
- - the locking/unlocking button in the centre console.
The TEG remote has 3 buttons which allow the operation of the central locking system: a button for unlocking the doors, one for locking the vehicle and one for releasing the boot.
See descriptions 5520 ENGINE STARTING [→939003530 5520 ENGINE STARTING]
> Note: The fuel flap is also locked/unlocked at the same time as the doors, controlled by the same driver's door logic.
> Note: If the remote control fails, insert the metal insert (inside the key) in the lock in the driver's door and turn it.With the central locking on, pulling the interior opening lever for one of the doors causes the closure for all the doors to be released. If there is no electrical power supply the doors can be locked manually
The locks have an additional motor that carries out the dead lock function which allows the interior door opening handles to be mechanically disconnected so that it is no longer possible to open the door from the inside (for example, after having broken the glass in a theft attempt); the dead lock function also inhibits the operation of the door locking/unlocking buttons in the dashboard.
The dead lock function is switched on at the time the doors are locked or by pressing the remote control twice.
The LED in the driver's door produces the following signals:
- Locking the locks: the LED lights up for 3 seconds. If some of the doors or the boot are not properly shut at the time when the locks are locked, the LED flashes at 3 Hz for 3 seconds;
- Dead lock activation: the LED flashes twice for 0.5 seconds;
- Unlocking the locks: the LED goes out.
The doors are automatically unlocked if the inertia switch is operated: the instrument panel receives a signal from the switch, lights up the appropriate warning light and notifies the Body Computer via the CAN.

###### Possible adjustments
It is possible, using the special setup in the instrument panel, to select whether to unlock all the doors or only the driver's front door, whilst all the other doors and the boot remain locked.
It is possible to enable/disable the locking of the doors above a certain speed threshold (20 km/h) using the special setup in the instrument panel: in this case the Body Computer implements the locking of the doors when this threshold is exceeded.
When the speed returns below this level, the doors and the boot remain locked; later on, when one of the doors is opened, the function is re-enabled and, if the threshold is exceeded, the doors are locked once again.
The boot unlocking operating mode can be selected still using the special setup in the instrument panel:
- assisted boot unlocking: the tailgate is considered as a fifth door to all intents and purposes;
- indepedent boot unlocking: the boot is locked when the doors are locked, whilst it can be unlocked independently of the unlocking of the doors.

##### Electric rear windows
The electric windows in the rear doors are activated using the switches in the actual doors and the driver's front door.
Automatic operation takes place as follows:
- if the button is pressed is between 60 and 300 milliseconds, operation is manual. the glass goes up/down only with the key pressed;
- f the key is pressed for longer than 300 milliseconds, operation is automatic: even if the button is released, the glass continues to move up/down until the end of travel position is reached or until the intervention of the anti-crush safety system (if fitted);
- pressing the button again whilst the window is moving stops it in the position it is in;
- if the button is pressed for less than 60 milliseconds, this is ignored (it is treated as an accidental knock).
The luggage compartment junction unit also manages the anti-crush safety function: it acquires information concerning the possible presence of an obstacle whilst the glass is closing: under these circumstances the control unit immediately interrupts the travel of the window and reverses it to the lower end of travel position.
> Note: If a failure is detected in the system or if the anti-crush safety function is activated 3 times in the space of 1 minute or if there is a failure, the system automatically enters into recovery mode (self-protection).This condition is evident from the window closing by being raised in stages.
If this happens the system restoral procedure must be carried out as follows:
- open the windows;
- extract the key (TEG) from the starting device and then insert it again
The driver's front door control unit manages the locking of the rear controls (protection) when the special LOCK button is pressed: the locking status is indicated by an LED in the back of the actual button lighting up and the rear control buttons are not lit up. The electric windows cannot be operated using any of the buttons when the lock function is activated.

##### Child-locks
The rear doors are fitted with a locking device that prevents them from being opened from the inside.
The device can only be switched on/off (using the metal insert in the key) with the doors open.
